    AATP · Chapter 0

    Start here: what AATP is

    AATP answers one question every time a customer orders: how much can we promise, and by what date?

    ATP and AATP

    ATP means Available-to-Promise. It is the check SAP runs when you save a sales order. It looks at stock and expected receipts and says "yes, 600 pieces on Monday".

    AATP (Advanced ATP) is the newer version inside S/4HANA. It does the same check faster, and adds business rules on top: who should get stock first, how much each region may take, what to do when the plant is short.

    Question from the businessClassic ATP (same as ECC)AATP
    Is stock available for this order?YesYes, faster
    Can each region have a fixed share of short stock?Old SD product allocation, hard to maintainProduct Allocation
    Can we keep some stock aside for one channel?NoSupply Protection
    Can important orders take stock from less important ones?Rescheduling (V_V2), first come first servedBackorder Processing with priorities
    Can the system offer another plant or product by itself?NoAlternative-Based Confirmation
    Can we tie exact stock to an exact order?NoSupply Assignment
    Can we promise based on a real production plan?NoSupply Creation-Based Confirmation

    The parts of AATP

    AATP is not one feature. It is a family. This course has one chapter for each part.

    PartShort nameWhat it does in one line
    Product Availability CheckPACChecks stock and expected receipts
    Product AllocationPALSets a maximum each group may take
    Supply ProtectionSUPKeeps a minimum aside for a group
    Backorder ProcessingBOPRe-shares confirmations between open orders by priority
    Alternative-Based ConfirmationABCTries another plant or another product
    Supply Assignment and Release for DeliveryARun, RefDyTies exact supply to exact orders, then releases them
    Supply Creation-Based ConfirmationSBCPlans new production to confirm the order

    How AATP is switched on

    1. Every product has a checking group on its master record (field "Availability check").
    2. In the checking group setup (transaction OVZ2, "Define Checking Groups") there is a field Advanced ATP. Set it to Active.
    3. All products with that checking group now use AATP. Products with other checking groups stay on classic ATP.

    So you can start small: create one new checking group, switch AATP on for it, and give it only to the products that need it.

    Check the licence first On S/4HANA on-premise and private cloud, AATP must be activated and needs an additional licence from SAP. On public cloud, AATP is the only version; basic features are in the standard licence and the advanced ones need the extra licence. Ask the client's SAP account manager before you design anything.
    One side effect Once a product uses AATP, the old rescheduling transactions (V_V2, V_RA, CO06) no longer work for it. You must set up Backorder Processing (Chapter 4) to replace them.

    Two things every part shares

    Characteristics
    These are order fields you use to write rules, such as sales organisation, region, customer group, customer or product. Allocation, protection, alternatives and backorder rules all use them. You choose which fields are available in the characteristic catalog apps.
    Review Availability Check Result (app F4719)
    This screen explains a confirmation step by step: what availability gave, what allocation gave, what protection held back. Use it whenever a user asks "why did I get only this much?"

    The example used in this course

    All scenarios use a chocolate company. It makes chocolate bars and festive gift boxes, stores them in depots (Chennai, Bengaluru, Delhi) and sells to distributors (general trade), big retail chains (modern trade) and e-commerce sites.

    Go deeper: foundation setup

    The sections below are the hands-on level. They follow S/4HANA 2023 (on-premise and private cloud). Field labels and menu positions can differ a little in other releases, so read the screen in front of you. Open each section when you are ready for it.

    Customising: switching AATP on, field by field

    Menu: SPRO > Cross-Application Components > Advanced Available-to-Promise (aATP). Transaction ATP_IMG opens this menu directly.

    Step 1. Check the business function

    Transaction SFW5. In the always-on functions, S4H_AATP should show as active. Nothing to change; this is only a check.

    Step 2. Define the checking group

    Menu: aATP > Product Availability Check (PAC) > Define Availability Check Group (same table as transaction OVZ2)

    FieldWhat it meansExample
    AvTwo-character key of the groupZ1
    DescriptionFree textAATP finished goods
    TotalSalesHow sales order requirements are stored: A = each order line as its own record; B = one total per dayA. AATP needs each order line separately.
    TotDlvReqsThe same choice for delivery requirementsA
    Block QtRqBlocks the checked quantity while a user is in the order, so two users cannot promise the same piecesTicked
    No checkSwitches the check off for the whole groupEmpty
    Accumul.Guards against over-confirming when earlier orders were confirmed against later receipts3 is a common choice. Agree it with the planning team.
    RelChkPlanOnly for the check against planningEmpty
    Advanced ATPThe main switchActive

    Step 3. Default checking group (optional)

    "Configure Default Values for Availability Check Group" proposes a group when a new product is created, per material type and plant. Useful when all finished goods should get Z1.

    Step 4. Put the group on the product

    Product master, MRP 3 view (or Sales: General/Plant), field "Availability check" = Z1. This is plant-specific, so repeat for each plant.

    App walkthrough: Manage Characteristic Catalogs (F3829)

    This app decides which order fields can be used in rules. Do it once, before any allocation, protection, backorder or alternative setup.

    1. Open the app. You see one catalog for each use: Product Allocation, Supply Protection, Backorder Processing, Alternative-Based Confirmation. There are catalogs for sales documents, for stock transport orders, and mixed ones for both.
    2. Open the catalog you need and choose Edit.
    3. Add the fields the business rules need. Typical picks: Sales Organization, Distribution Channel, Customer Group, Region, Sold-to Party, Delivery Priority, Plant.
    4. Optional: rename a field so users understand it.
    5. Optional: create value groups, for example a group "Priority 1 customers" that lists ten sold-to parties. Rules can then use the group.
    6. Save. The fields now appear in the selection lists of the other apps.
    Good to know
    • Remove fields you will not use. Short lists are easier for the business users.
    • A custom field must first be created in "Custom Fields and Logic" and enabled for the right business context. Until then it does not appear here.
    • Not every standard order field is offered. If a field is missing, check SAP KBA 3086331 before promising it to the client.
    • Users need the business role Order Fulfillment Manager (R0226) to see the AATP configuration apps.

    AATP · Chapter 1

    Product Availability Check

    The base of everything. It decides how much stock is free to promise, and on which date.

    Business scenario A distributor orders 800 cartons of milk chocolate bars today. The plant has 600 in stock. Production will bring 400 more on day 5. Another customer already holds a confirmed order for 300, to be delivered on day 3. How much can we promise the new order?

    The basic sum

    Free to promise = stock + expected receipts − already promised

    • Stock: what is physically in the plant.
    • Expected receipts: production orders, purchase orders, planned orders.
    • Already promised: other sales orders, deliveries, reservations.

    Stock promised to someone else is gone, even if their delivery is a few days away.

    The three settings that control the check

    1. Checking group (on the product)
    Says how this product is checked, and whether AATP is on for it.
    2. Checking rule (from the transaction)
    A sales order uses rule A. A delivery uses rule B. So the same product can be checked one way at order time and another way at delivery time.
    3. Scope of check (checking group + checking rule, transaction OVZ9)
    A list of tick-boxes that says what to count.
    Group of tick-boxesExamplesThink about
    Which stockSafety stock, quality inspection stock, blocked stock, stock in transitQuality stock may fail. Counting it means you may promise goods you cannot ship.
    Which receiptsPurchase orders, production orders, planned orders, purchase requisitionsA released production order is reliable. A planned order is only a plan.
    Which issuesSales orders, deliveries, reservations, dependent requirementsIf you leave sales orders out, the same stock gets promised twice.
    Replenishment lead timeOn or offSee below. This one causes the most trouble.

    Replenishment lead time

    This is the total time to make or buy the product, say 20 days.

    • Switched on: the system thinks "after 20 days I can always get more". It confirms any quantity at day 20, even when nothing is planned.
    • Switched off: the system confirms only against real stock and real receipts.
    Common complaint "The order was confirmed in full, but on the date there was no stock." Nine times out of ten, replenishment lead time is on and nobody planned production. For products that are often short, switch it off.

    How the date is worked out

    The system first works backward from the date the customer wants:

    Wanted delivery date − transit time − loading time − pick and pack time = date stock must be ready

    If stock is ready on that date, the wanted date is confirmed. If not, the system finds the first date stock is ready and works forward, adding the same times back.

    Transit time comes from the route. Loading time and pick and pack time come from the shipping point.

    What the user sees when stock is short

    • One-time delivery: take what is available on the wanted date, nothing more.
    • Complete delivery: everything together, on the first date the full quantity is available.
    • Delivery proposal: part deliveries, as stock becomes available.

    Which choices are allowed depends on the partial delivery agreement in the customer master.

    What AATP adds to this check

    • It is much faster on large order volumes.
    • Many users can check the same product at the same moment. The system holds a small temporary reservation for each user while they work, so nobody blocks anybody.
    • The result screen explains itself (Review Availability Check Result).

    Setup steps

    1. Define the checking group and set Advanced ATP to Active (OVZ2).
    2. Put the checking group on the product (MRP 3 view or Sales: General/Plant view).
    3. Set the scope of check for the checking group with rule A (order) and rule B (delivery) (OVZ9).
    4. Check that the requirement class and the schedule line category have both "availability check" and "transfer of requirements" switched on.
    5. Maintain transit time on routes and loading and pick and pack time on shipping points.
    6. Test with a few orders and read the result in Review Availability Check Result.

    Go deeper: configuration

    Hands-on level, following S/4HANA 2023. Open each section when you are ready.

    App walkthrough: Review Availability Check Result (F4719)
    1. Create or change a sales order and enter the line: product, quantity 800, wanted delivery date.
    2. Press Enter, or choose Check Availability. If the full quantity is not available on the wanted date, the result screen opens.
    3. Top area: the request (product, plant, quantity, wanted date) and the outcome (confirmed quantity and dates).
    4. Delivery proposals: the three choices from this chapter: one-time delivery, complete delivery, delivery proposal. Pick one and accept.
    5. Intermediate results: one block for each check that ran. Open "Product Availability" to see stock, receipts and what is already promised. If protection or allocation is active, each has its own details link.
    6. Accept the result. The schedule lines in the order now carry the confirmed quantities and dates.

    To see the same numbers outside an order, use the app Monitor Product Availability (the old CO09). Enter product, plant and checking rule A.

    AATP · Chapter 2

    Product Allocation

    A quota. It sets the most that each region, channel or customer may take in a period, even when stock is there.

    Business scenario Before Diwali, a new festive gift box is in high demand. The factory can make 50,000 boxes a month. On day one, a big distributor in the North orders 40,000. If the system confirms it, the South, West and East get almost nothing, and those distributors move to a competitor.

    The idea

    You decide in advance how the month's supply is shared. The availability check may say "50,000 available", but the allocation check says "North may take 15,000 this month". The order gets the lower of the two.

    The building blocks

    Product allocation object
    The container for one quota plan, for example "Festive gift box, by region". It holds the characteristics and the time period type (day, week or month).
    Characteristics
    What the quota is split by: sales organisation, region, customer group, customer, and so on. You can combine them, for example region and channel.
    Planning data
    The actual numbers: 15,000 for North in October, 15,000 in November. Entered in an app or uploaded from a file.
    Assignment
    Which product in which plant uses this object, and from which date to which date.
    Sequence
    Lets one product use more than one object. See below.

    Using quota from other periods

    • Backward consumption: if this month's quota is finished, the system may use quota left over from earlier months.
    • Forward consumption: the system may use next month's quota. The confirmed date then moves into next month.
    • Neither: each month stands alone. Unused quota is lost at month end.

    You set how many periods back and forward are allowed.

    Sequences: alternatives and constraints

    Alternatives (OR)
    "Try the customer's own quota first. If it is finished, use the region quota." The order may draw from one pot after another.
    Constraints (AND)
    "The order must fit in the region quota and in the channel quota." The order gets the smallest result of all the pots.

    Worth knowing

    • The quota is checked against a date. You choose whether that is the date stock must be ready or the wanted delivery date.
    • It works for sales orders and for stock transfer orders.
    • If stock itself is less than the quota, the order gets only the stock. Quota is a ceiling, not a guarantee.
    • Switching on AATP product allocation is a one-way step. You cannot go back to the old SD product allocation afterwards.

    Setup steps (apps)

    1. Activate product allocation in customising (once per client).
    2. Configure Product Allocation (F2119): create the object, pick the characteristics and period type.
    3. Manage Product Allocation Planning Data (F2121): enter the quantities for each value and period.
    4. Manage Product Allocation Sequences: only if you need alternatives or constraints.
    5. Assign Product to Product Allocation (F2120): link product and plant, with validity dates.
    6. Activate the object and test. Product Allocation Overview shows how much of each quota is used.
    Common mistakes
    • Quota left in place after the shortage is over. Stock sits in the warehouse while orders stay unconfirmed. Give every allocation an end date.
    • A customer or region with no planning data gets zero. Decide what "everyone else" should receive and plan it.
    • Too many characteristics. Region by channel by customer by week is a lot of numbers for someone to maintain. Start simple.

    Go deeper: configuration

    Hands-on level, following S/4HANA 2023. Open each section when you are ready.

    Customising: activating product allocation

    Menu: aATP > Product Allocation (PAL) > Activate Product Allocation

    SettingWhat it meansExample
    ActivateSwitches AATP product allocation on for the whole clientYes
    Check dateWhich order date picks the quota period: material availability date or requested delivery dateRequested delivery date, if the business plans quota by when the customer receives goods
    Before you press save
    • It is per client and cannot be undone. The old SD product allocation stops being used.
    • No old allocation data and no existing confirmations are carried over. Plan the first load of quota numbers.
    • The checking group of the product must already have Advanced ATP active.

    Also tick "Prod. allocation" in the requirement class (OVZG) and the schedule line category (VOV6). Without these the order line never asks for a quota check.

    App walkthrough 1: Configure Product Allocation (F2119)

    Choose Create and fill the header.

    FieldWhat it meansExample
    Name and descriptionYour name for the objectPAL_GIFTBOX_REGION, "Festive gift box by region"
    Quantity unitUnit of the quota numbersPC
    Period typeDay, week, month, quarter or year. One type only.Month
    Time zone and factory calendarDecide where a period starts and endsIndia, your sales calendar
    Check dateWhich order date finds the periodRequested delivery date
    Document relevanceSales orders, stock transport orders, or bothSales orders
    Collective allocationWhat happens to orders whose values have no own quota line: No collective allocation = only exact matches get quota; Managed manually = you maintain a catch-all line marked #; Managed by system = the system creates the catch-all linesManaged manually, so "all other regions" can share one line
    CharacteristicsThe fields the quota is split by, in orderSales Organization, Region

    App walkthrough 2: Manage Product Allocation Planning Data (F2121)
    1. Open the object PAL_GIFTBOX_REGION.
    2. Add one line for each value combination: 1000 / North, 1000 / South, 1000 / West, 1000 / East, and 1000 / # for all others.
    3. Enter the planned quantity for each period: North 15,000 for October, 15,000 for November, and so on.
    4. For many lines, download the grid to a spreadsheet, fill it and upload it.
    5. Save. For each line and period the app shows planned, consumed and still available quantity.

    Each line also carries a constraint status, which you can change here or on the sequence, depending on release:

    StatusEffect on the order
    Restricted availabilityNormal case. The planned quantities limit the order.
    Unrestricted availabilityNo limit. Useful to "open" one region for a while without deleting numbers.
    No availabilityNothing is confirmed.
    Not relevantThis constraint is skipped.
    App walkthrough 3: Manage Product Allocation Sequences

    The sequence is the top object. It links products to one or more allocation objects.

    LevelFieldsExample
    Sequence headerName, unit, backward consumption periods, forward consumption periodsSEQ_GIFTBOX, PC, backward 1, forward 0
    Sequence groupNumber (order of trying), optional own consumption periods. Groups are the alternatives: the system tries group 10 first, then 20.10 = key account quota; 20 = region quota
    Constraint inside a groupNumber, description, one allocation object, allocation rate, validity from and to, constraint status. All constraints in one group must be met together.Object PAL_GIFTBOX_REGION, rate 1.0, valid 1 Oct to 31 Dec, restricted availability
    • One group with one constraint is the simple case from this chapter.
    • Two constraints in one group = AND. Two groups = OR.
    • Keep the allocation rate at 1.0 unless one order piece should use more or less than one quota piece.
    • The validity dates are your safety net. A constraint that has ended no longer limits orders.
    App walkthrough 4: Assign Product to Product Allocation (F2120)
    1. Choose the allocation object (and, where your release asks for it, the sequence).
    2. Add the product and plant, with valid-from and valid-to dates.
    3. Save.
    Shared pot warning The planned numbers belong to the object, not to one product. If you assign three products to the same object, all three draw from the same 15,000. If each product needs its own quota, add Product as a characteristic or create one object per product.

    Watching usage

    • Product Allocation Overview (F3474): planned, consumed and available per line and period.
    • Monitor Product Allocation Characteristic Value Combinations (F3476): the same, as a list for many objects.
    • Monitor Product Allocation Order Items (F3477): which order lines used which quota.

    AATP · Chapter 3

    Supply Protection

    The opposite of a quota. It keeps a minimum quantity aside for one group, so that other orders cannot use it.

    Business scenario The plant has 10,000 pieces. Your contract with an e-commerce site says you must always be able to ship 2,000 a week, or you pay a penalty. General trade distributors order early in the week and usually take everything.

    The idea

    You tell the system "2,000 pieces of this product in this plant are protected for e-commerce". When any other customer orders, the availability check behaves as if those 2,000 are not there.

    How it behaves

    • When the protected group orders, its protected quantity is used first. It can also take open stock if there is any.
    • Every other group sees: free stock minus what is protected for others.
    • Protection is planned per time period, for example per week. You can protect more in festival weeks and less afterwards.
    • When a period ends, protection that was not used expires. That stock becomes free for everyone.
    • It works for sales orders and stock transfer orders, and the backorder run respects it.

    Quota or protection? The difference

    Product AllocationSupply Protection
    What it setsA maximum a group may takeA minimum kept for a group
    Business sentence"North must not take more than 15,000""E-commerce must always find 2,000"
    Who is limitedThe group itselfEveryone else
    Based onPlanned numbers, separate from stockReal supply of a product in a plant
    Typical useFair sharing during a shortageContracts, penalties, key channels

    You can use both together. Protection lowers what availability returns. Allocation then caps the result.

    The building blocks

    Supply protection object
    Created for one product in one plant.
    Protection groups
    Who is protected, described with characteristics. Example: distribution channel = e-commerce. One object can hold several groups.
    Protected quantity per period
    The number to hold back in each week or month.
    Priority levels
    If supply is too small to protect everybody, a prioritised characteristic decides which group is served first.

    Setup steps

    1. Make sure the fields you need (channel, customer group and so on) are available as characteristics.
    2. Manage Supply Protection (F4569): create the object for product and plant.
    3. Add the protection groups and their values.
    4. Enter the protected quantity for each period.
    5. Activate, then test with one order from inside the group and one from outside.
    Common mistakes
    • Protecting too much. Stock sits idle while other customers stay unconfirmed. Review the numbers every planning cycle.
    • One order matching two protection groups. Design the groups so that an order can belong to only one.
    • Using protection when the business really wants a ceiling. Listen for "at least" (protection) or "at most" (allocation).

    Go deeper: configuration

    Hands-on level, following S/4HANA 2023. Open each section when you are ready.

    Customising and prerequisites
    • The product's checking group has Advanced ATP active.
    • In Configure Scope of Availability Check, the supply protection option is switched on for the checking group and rule (Chapter 1, last row of the table).
    • The fields you want to protect by are in the Supply Protection catalog (Manage Characteristic Catalogs).

    There is no other customising. The rest is one app.

    App walkthrough: Manage Supply Protection (F4569)

    Choose Create.

    FieldWhat it meansExample
    Name and descriptionYour name for the objectSUP_GIFTBOX_ECOM
    Material and plantOne object protects one product in one plantGB-100, plant 1000
    UnitUnit of the protected quantityPC
    Planning period typeDay, week, month or quarter. One type for each object.Week
    Planning start and endThe horizon the protection covers. The number of periods is limited (SAP KBA 3649071), so do not plan years ahead in days.This week to end of the festival month
    Consumption based onWhich order date decides the period an order consumes: material availability date or requested delivery dateRequested delivery date
    Restriction by own protectionWhether the protected group itself is held back by its protection in other periods. Options: no restriction; restriction outside planning horizon; restriction outside time bucket; from 2023 also restriction outside planned protection.No restriction to start. Use "outside time bucket" when each week's quantity must stay for that week.
    Characteristic 1 (and 2)The core fields that define a protection group. One is required, two are allowed.Distribution Channel
    Prioritized characteristicsOptional extra fields used to rank groupsCustomer Group

    Then add the protection groups:

    FieldWhat it meansExample
    Priority1 is highest. A higher group may ignore the protection of lower groups. A lower group must respect equal and higher ones.1
    Characteristic valuesWho belongs to the groupDistribution Channel = 30 (e-commerce)
    Protected quantity per periodHow much to hold in each week2,000 each week

    Save and choose Activate. Only an active object takes part in the check.

    Two ways of protecting

    Core protection (side by side)
    Groups protect against each other. Each keeps its own quantity. Use it when no group is more important than another.
    Prioritised protection (ranked)
    Groups have priorities. Orders in a higher group can use stock protected for lower groups, but not the other way round.

    What happens over time

    • An order from the protected group consumes the protection of the period its date falls in.
    • When a period's end date passes, whatever was not consumed expires and the stock becomes free for everyone.
    • Two different protection objects for the same product and plant always hold their full quantities against each other.

    Where to see it

    • In the order: Review Availability Check Result, intermediate results, details for supply protection.
    • The object itself shows protected and consumed quantity for each period.
    • Supply Demand Overview shows protected quantities next to real orders.
    Test script

    Prepare: stock 10,000, object as above with 2,000 for this week, activated.

    No.StepExpected result
    3.1General trade order (channel 10) for 9,0008,000 confirmed. Details show 2,000 held by protection.
    3.2E-commerce order (channel 30) for 1,5001,500 confirmed; consumed quantity in the object becomes 1,500
    3.3Second e-commerce order for 1,000500 confirmed
    3.4Deactivate the object, recheck order 3.1Any stock that is still unconfirmed becomes available to it
    3.5Reactivate; create a period that ends yesterday with 1,000 unconsumed; check a general trade orderThe 1,000 from the past period no longer restricts
    3.6Stock transport order from this plant, if STOs are in scopeIt respects the protection too
    Troubleshooting
    SymptomLikely causeFix
    Protection has no effectObject not activated; scope of check option not switched on; order date outside the planning horizonCheck each
    Protected group itself is not confirmed"Restriction by own protection" is set tight and the order date falls in another periodReview that setting
    Everyone else is short while stock sitsProtected quantity too high, or long periods that have not expired yetLower the numbers; use shorter periods
    An order matches two groupsOverlapping valuesRedesign so each order fits one group
    Consumed is more than protected in one period, less in anotherConsumption is posted to the matching period onlyExpected. A BAdI exists to spread it if needed.
    Value list for a field is empty in the appField not properly in the catalogManage Characteristic Catalogs; see SAP KBA 3781757

    AATP · Chapter 4

    Backorder Processing

    A job that looks at all open orders together and re-shares the confirmations by business priority.

    Business scenario Yesterday a small retailer's order took 300 of the last pieces. Today a key modern trade customer orders 400 of the same item, urgently. Also, one customer with confirmed stock has just gone on credit block. Nothing changes by itself: the urgent order shows zero.

    Why it is needed

    SAP confirms orders first come, first served. After an order is saved, the system never rechecks it on its own. So confirmations go out of date when:

    • an important order arrives late,
    • production comes early or late,
    • an order is cancelled or blocked and its stock should go to someone else.

    Backorder processing fixes this. It usually runs every night.

    The building blocks

    Segment
    A named group of order lines, chosen by a filter, with a sort order inside it. Example: "Modern trade orders due this week, oldest first".
    Confirmation strategy
    How a segment is treated in the run. There are seven (table below).
    Variant
    The full recipe for one run: which segments, and which strategy for each.
    Run
    The job that executes a variant. It can run for real or as a simulation that changes nothing.

    The seven strategies

    StrategyWhat happens to these ordersTypical use
    WinMust be confirmed in full on the wanted date. If that is impossible, the run reports a problem.Rush orders, top key accounts
    GainKeep at least what they have. Get more if possible. If they cannot keep it, the run reports a problem.Priority customers with orders due soon
    ImproveTry to keep and improve, but may lose if higher groups need the stock. No problem is reported. Added in release 2022.Good customers you would like to help, without a hard promise
    RedistributeMay end up better, the same or worse.All normal orders
    FillNever get more. Keep what they have, or lose some.Low priority orders, internal stock transfers
    LoseLose all confirmation.Credit-blocked customers
    SkipLeft out of the run. Stay exactly as they are.Orders you do not want touched

    The run serves Win first, then Gain, then the middle groups, then Fill. Stock freed from Lose orders goes to the groups above.

    Sorting inside a segment

    When two orders in the same segment compete, the sort order decides. Common choices: wanted delivery date, order creation date, delivery priority from the customer master. If the standard fields are not enough, the app Configure Custom BOP Sorting lets you define your own order of values.

    Setup steps (apps)

    1. Agree the priority rules with the business first. This is the hard part.
    2. Configure BOP Segment (F2158): create one segment for each group, with filter and sort.
    3. Configure BOP Variant (F2160): put the segments under the right strategies.
    4. Schedule BOP Run (F2665): run it in simulation first, then schedule the real job.
    5. Monitor BOP Run (F2159): see which orders gained, which lost, and any problems.

    When to run it

    After the night's planning run and goods receipts, and before delivery creation in the morning. Some businesses add a second run at midday.

    Common mistakes
    • Putting too many orders in Win. If everything is top priority, nothing is.
    • Forgetting the customer side. An order that loses its confirmation may already have been promised by phone. Agree who informs the customer.
    • No simulation before go-live. Always simulate and read the monitor with the sales head.

    Go deeper: configuration

    Hands-on level, following S/4HANA 2023. Backorder processing has no customising of its own; everything is in the apps. Open each section when you are ready.

    Prerequisites
    • Products are on a checking group with Advanced ATP active.
    • The fields you want to filter and sort by are in the Backorder Processing catalog.
    • The person who configures has the role Order Fulfillment Manager (R0226).
    • Old rescheduling jobs for these products are stopped.
    App walkthrough 1: Configure BOP Segment (F2158)

    Create one segment for each group of orders the business names.

    PartWhat you enterExample: segment MT_DUE_7_DAYS
    Name and descriptionUse names the business understands"Modern trade, due within 7 days"
    Selection criteriaOne or more conditions: field, comparison, value. Joined with AND or OR.Customer Group is equal to "MT" AND Requested Delivery Date is within the next 7 days
    Exclusion conditionsOptional. Orders that match are left out.Sales Document Type is equal to sample order
    PrioritizersThe sort order inside the segment: field and ascending or descending. Several are allowed; the first is the main sort.1. Delivery Priority ascending; 2. Requested Delivery Date ascending; 3. Creation Date ascending
    • The condition editor works with typed values and simple comparisons. You cannot upload a long list of values (SAP KBA 3741015). For lists, create a value group in the characteristic catalog and filter on the group.
    • If plain ascending or descending is not enough, for example "customer B before customer A before customer C", define the order in Configure Custom BOP Sorting (F2983) and pick it as a prioritizer.
    App walkthrough 2: Configure BOP Variant (F2160)
    PartWhat it meansExample: variant NIGHTLY_FG
    Name and description"Nightly run, finished goods"
    Document typesSales orders, stock transport orders, or bothBoth
    Execution methodProduct availability check (normal) or supply assignment (Chapter 6)Product availability check
    Global filterOptional segment that limits the whole runSegment "Plant 1000 and 2000 only"
    Exception behaviourWhat to do when a Win or Gain order cannot get what it must: stop processing only that product and plant, or stop the whole runStop that product and plant only
    Fallback variantA second, simpler variant that then runs for the stopped products, so they are not left untouchedVariant FALLBACK_REDISTRIBUTE with everything under Redistribute
    StrategiesDrag each segment under Win, Gain, Improve, Redistribute, Fill, Lose or Skip. Several segments can sit under one strategy; they are processed top to bottom.See the sample below

    Sample variant for the chocolate company

    StrategySegmentSort
    WinRush orders; e-commerce orders due in 2 daysRequested date
    GainModern trade due in 7 daysDelivery priority, then date
    RedistributeAll other sales orders due in 14 daysRequested date, then creation date
    FillStock transport orders to depots; orders due later than 14 daysRequested date
    LoseCustomers on credit blockNone
    SkipFree sample ordersNone

    Use the Simulate button in the variant to try it at once without changing orders.

    App walkthrough 3: Schedule BOP Run (F2665) and Monitor BOP Run (F2159)

    Schedule

    1. Create a new job from the template for backorder runs.
    2. Pick the variant, for example NIGHTLY_FG.
    3. Tick simulation for a trial run; leave it empty for a real run.
    4. Set the start: immediately, or a time such as 02:00 with daily recurrence.
    5. Schedule. The job list shows status and log.

    Monitor

    1. The first screen lists the runs: variant, start time, status, real or simulation.
    2. Open a run. You see totals by strategy: how many order lines, how many fully, partly or not confirmed.
    3. Drill into a strategy, then a product and plant, then the order lines.
    4. For each line: wanted quantity, confirmed before, confirmed after, and whether it gained or lost.
    5. Exceptions are flagged, for example a Win order that could not be confirmed. If an alternative plant was used (Chapter 5), the line carries a marker.

    Make reading this monitor a daily task for one named person.

    Test script

    Prepare: stock 1,000. Orders: A key account 400 (created last, 0 confirmed), B normal 500 (500 confirmed), C small retailer 300 (300 confirmed), D 200 (200 confirmed) from a customer you then credit-block. Segments so that A is Win, B Redistribute, C Fill, D Lose.

    No.StepExpected result
    4.1Run the variant in simulationMonitor shows A 400, B 500, C 100, D 0. Orders unchanged.
    4.2Run for realSame result; schedule lines in the orders are updated
    4.3Move A's segment from Win to Gain and add order E (Win) for 1,200E cannot be fully confirmed: exception; fallback variant runs for this product
    4.4Post a goods receipt of 300 and run againC stays at 100. Fill never gains. To let C recover, its segment must sit under Redistribute or Improve.
    4.5Put a sample order under Skip, runIts confirmation is untouched
    4.6Run while a user has order B open in change modeB cannot be updated and is reported with an update problem; others are processed
    Troubleshooting
    SymptomLikely causeFix
    An order is not picked upIts document type is not in the variant; it matches no segment; the global filter excludes it; the product is not on AATPCheck in that order. Simulate with a filter on the one order.
    Monitor shows a confirmed quantity but the order has no confirmed schedule lineThe order failed the credit check when the result was written backRelease credit, then rerun
    Orders are locked for a long time during the runLarge run during working hoursRun at night; split by plant with global filters
    Run stops with exceptionsWin or Gain orders ask for more than existsMove fewer orders into Win; set a fallback variant
    Results change from night to night for no clear reasonSorting uses a field with equal values, so order is arbitraryAdd a final prioritizer such as creation date
    Order is not confirmed from another plant though that plant has stockEarlier orders in the same run took it; or the original product's quota is used upRead the monitor for that plant; check quota
    "Variant not found" in the jobVariant renamed or deleted after schedulingReschedule with the current variant

    AATP · Chapter 5

    Alternative-Based Confirmation

    When the asked plant cannot deliver in full and on time, the system looks at other plants, or at a replacement product, by itself.

    Business scenario A customer near Chennai orders 2,000 pieces. The Chennai depot has 500. The Bengaluru depot has 3,000. Today the order desk phones around, then changes the plant in the order by hand. Sometimes nobody notices and the customer waits two weeks.

    The idea

    For orders you choose, the system checks a list of alternative plants at the same moment as the normal check, compares the results, and confirms from the best one.

    Two kinds of alternative

    Plant substitution
    Same product, different plant or depot.
    Product substitution
    Different product, for example the new pack that replaces an old one, or the same bar under a new article number. Which product may replace which is kept as substitution master data.

    Newer releases can combine both: another product from another plant.

    The two decisions you configure

    1. Who gets alternatives (alternative control)
    Not every order should be allowed to switch plant. You use characteristics to say which ones may: for example only modern trade customers, or only certain product groups.
    2. How to choose between alternatives (substitution strategy)
    The rule for picking a winner. Examples: prefer the asked plant if it can deliver in full; otherwise prefer the plant that can deliver everything on time; otherwise split across as few plants as possible.

    What the user sees

    • If the whole line moves, the plant on the order line changes.
    • If the line is split, the system creates sub-items under the main line, one for each plant, each with its own quantity and date.
    • Every alternative is checked fully: availability, protection and allocation all apply in the other plant too.
    Check these before you switch it on in India
    • GST: the delivering plant decides the tax. Chennai to a Tamil Nadu customer is CGST and SGST. Bengaluru to the same customer is IGST. Pricing and invoicing must handle both.
    • Freight: a farther depot costs more. Decide who pays.
    • Master data: the product must be set up in every alternative plant, with shipping point and route determination working from there.
    • Customer rules: some customers accept only one delivery, or only from one depot.

    Setup steps (apps)

    1. List which plants may stand in for which, and for which customers. Agree it with sales and logistics.
    2. Configure Substitution Strategy (F2699): define how alternatives are found and ranked.
    3. Configure Alternative Control (F2698): say which orders use which strategy, by characteristic values.
    4. Newer releases also offer Manage Characteristic Combinations (F5303) and Configure Alternative Determination (F5354) for finer rules.
    5. Test with orders that should switch and orders that should not.

    App names and options differ a little between releases. Check what your system has.

    Go deeper: configuration

    Hands-on level, following S/4HANA 2023. This part of AATP has changed most between releases, so compare with your system. Open each section when you are ready.

    Customising and prerequisites

    Item categories for sub-items (on-premise)SD > Sales > Sales Documents > Sales Document Item > Assign Item Categories. For your order type and item category group, entries with usage ABC0 to ABC2 must exist, so the system can create the main item and its sub-items. SAP's standard example is TAPA for the main item and TAN for sub-items.
    Pricing and billing of sub-itemsDecide which level carries price and tax. Test the invoice.
    Product in every alternative plantSales and plant views, checking group with AATP active, shipping point and route determination
    Characteristic catalogFields for the control rules are in the Alternative-Based Confirmation catalog
    Substitution master dataFor product substitution: which product replaces which, with validity, kept in the substitution apps. For plant substitution: the list of allowed plants.
    App walkthrough 1: Configure Substitution Strategy (F2699)
    FieldWhat it meansExample: strategy DEPOT_SWITCH
    Name and description"Nearest depot with stock"
    Substitution item typeInline: the plant is changed on the same line; only one plant, only plant substitution. Sub-item: the line gets sub-items, needed for splits and product substitution. Or allow both.Allow both
    Remaining open quantityWhere any unconfirmed rest stays: on the original plant or product, or on the leading substituteOriginal request
    Consider alternativesAlways; or only for new lines; or only when saved lines are rechecked (change, backorder run)Always
    Substitution methodsWhat may be replaced and in which order: plant, storage location, product. Each with its source of substitutes.1. Plant: 1000, 2000, 3000
    Building ruleOne or more alternative determinations, tried in order. They decide which alternative wins.1. Full Confirmation; 2. Maximum Confirmation Earlier

    The delivered alternative determinations

    NameWhat it prefers
    On-Time ConfirmationOnly what can be delivered on the wanted date, as much as possible that day
    Full ConfirmationThe full quantity or nothing. Among equal choices, the smallest delay and the fewest plants.
    Maximum Confirmation EarlierThe largest quantity as early as possible

    If the first determination finds nothing, the next one is tried. In Configure Alternative Determination (F5354) you can copy these and add a hard limit such as "maximum delay 3 days".

    App walkthrough 2: Configure Alternative Control (F2698)
    1. Choose the fields that decide who gets alternatives, in order. Example: Sales Organization, Customer Group.
    2. Add value lines and give each a substitution strategy: 1000 / MT = DEPOT_SWITCH.
    3. Leave general trade without a line, so those orders stay on their plant.
    4. Activate.
    Entry traps
    • Some values need the internal key. Order type "OR" is stored as "TA".
    • Numeric keys need their full length with leading zeros, for example a ship-to as 0000123456.
    • An order must find exactly one strategy. If two lines match, nothing is substituted.
    Test script

    Prepare: product in plants 1000 (stock 500) and 2000 (stock 3,000). Strategy as above. Control line for customer group MT only.

    No.StepExpected result
    5.1MT customer orders 2,000 from plant 1000Confirmed 2,000 from plant 2000
    5.2General trade customer orders 2,000 from plant 1000500 confirmed in plant 1000; no switch
    5.3Change the building rule to Maximum Confirmation Earlier with sub-items; MT orders 3,200Sub-items: 500 from 1000 and 2,700 from 2000
    5.4Create delivery and invoice for 5.1 to an in-state and an out-of-state customerCorrect shipping point, correct GST type on each invoice
    5.5Put a quota on plant 2000 that is used up; repeat 5.1No switch; quota applies in the alternative plant too
    5.6Run the backorder variant after stock arrives in plant 1000Behaviour follows "Consider alternatives"; the monitor marks plant changes
    Troubleshooting
    SymptomLikely causeFix
    Nothing is substitutedOrder type or item category not supported; item category usage entries missing; "Consider alternatives" excludes this situationCheck prerequisites and the strategy
    Control line does not matchInternal value or leading zeros wrongEnter TA for OR; pad numbers to full length
    Still nothing though values are rightMore than one strategy foundMake the control lines unambiguous
    Product is never replacedA hard constraint in the determination forces the original product; or the original is not actually shortReview Configure Alternative Determination
    Result screen shows no alternativesAlternative plant missing master data or its own checks give zeroCheck the product, quota and protection in that plant
    Sub-item quantities look roundedThe delivery unit on the product's sales view is appliedExpected; adjust the delivery unit if wrong

    AATP · Chapter 6

    Supply Assignment and Release for Delivery

    Confirmation says "you will get 400". Assignment says "these exact 400 pieces are yours". Release decides when the order is complete enough to ship.

    Business scenario Distributors book the Diwali festive range three months ahead, before it is made. One order has four flavours: Milk, Dark, Hazelnut and Almond, 100 cartons each. Milk and Dark are in the warehouse. Hazelnut comes from production in six days. Almond is not planned yet. The warehouse ships the two flavours it has. The distributor is unhappy: half a festive range does not fill his shelves.

    Confirmation and assignment are different things

    Availability check (confirmation)Supply assignment
    Looks atThe total pool: all stock and receipts against all ordersOne order line and one specific supply
    ResultA quantity and a dateA fixed link: this stock or this production order belongs to this order line
    How long it holdsUntil someone rechecksUntil the delivery is made, unless you remove it

    Supply assignment came from SAP's fashion solutions, where it was called the allocation run. That is why its short name is still ARun. The idea works the same way for any seasonal range that customers book before it is made.

    How it works

    1. The product is marked as relevant for supply assignment in the plant (a field on the product master).
    2. A supply assignment rule says how supply and orders are matched: which supply types may be used and in what order.
    3. The assignment runs as part of a backorder run. So the same segments and priorities from Chapter 4 decide who is served first.
    4. Each order line gets a status. Linked to stock in the warehouse: fixed, ready for delivery. Linked to a future receipt such as a purchase or production order: reserved. Put aside for now: on hold.
    5. An optional release check looks at how complete the order is. A release rule sets two percentages, one for the whole order and one for each line, for example 90% and 80%. Only orders that pass get a delivery.

    Apps

    • Configure Supply Assignment Rules: the matching rules.
    • Monitor Supply Assignment Runs (F3684) and Monitor Supply Assignment Demand: what the run did.
    • Supply Demand Overview: supply and demand side by side, with what is assigned.
    • Adjust Supply Assignment (also called Insight to Action, transaction ARUNITA): assign, unassign, release or block by hand.
    • Maintain Release Rules: the percentages for the release check.
    Scope note Supply assignment belongs to the fashion and vertical business part of S/4HANA. Before proposing it, check that the client's system and licence include it, and that the products are set up for it.

    Release for Delivery

    This is a separate, simpler tool for the last step before shipping. It does not need supply assignment.

    Business scenario At 5 pm the dispatch manager learns that a key customer's truck leaves tonight. His order is short by 200. Another order with 200 confirmed is not leaving until next week.
    • The Release for Delivery app (F1786) shows the manager all orders that are due, with wanted and confirmed quantities.
    • He can move confirmed quantity from one order to another on the screen and see the effect at once.
    • When he is satisfied, he releases, and deliveries can be created for those orders.
    • Configure Order Fulfillment Responsibilities (F2246) decides which products and plants each manager sees.

    Think of backorder processing as the automatic nightly decision, and Release for Delivery as the human correction during the day.

    Go deeper: configuration

    Hands-on level, following S/4HANA 2023 with the fashion and vertical business functions. Open each section when you are ready.

    Setup steps for supply assignment, in order
    No.WhereWhat to doExample
    1Product master, plant dataMark the product as relevant for supply assignment in the plantFestive range products, plant 1000
    2Configure Supply Assignment RulesCreate a rule: which supply may be used (warehouse stock, purchase orders, production orders, inbound deliveries) and in what order; tick "Release check required" if you want step 6. A rule is mandatory from release 2020.Rule SA_DIWALI: stock first, then production orders by date; release check required
    3Configure BOP SegmentSegments that pick and sort the orders, as in Chapter 4Pre-booked Diwali orders, by delivery priority then requested date
    4Configure BOP VariantExecution method = Supply assignment; enter the rule; put segments under strategiesVariant SA_DIWALI_NIGHTLY
    5Schedule BOP RunRun it. Results: Monitor Supply Assignment Runs (F3684) and Monitor Supply Assignment Demand.Nightly
    6Maintain Release RulesHeader fulfilment % (whole order) and item fulfilment % (each line)Header 90, item 80

    The release check is optional. Without it, orders can be delivered as soon as stock is assigned.

    App walkthrough: Release for Delivery (F1786)

    One-time setup

    Configure Order Fulfillment Responsibilities (F2246): create a responsibility for each dispatch manager, with selection criteria such as plant or product group. You can create several in one step. This decides what each manager sees.

    Daily use

    1. Open the app. It lists products in your responsibility that have orders due and not enough supply.
    2. Open a product. You see the due order lines with wanted and confirmed quantity, and the supply available for the day.
    3. Change confirmed quantities by typing or with the quick actions, for example confirm from the top of the list. The totals update as you go, so you cannot give out more than exists.
    4. You can protect a line from further change, or postpone it.
    5. Choose Release for Delivery. The orders are updated and delivery creation can pick them up.
    Test script

    Prepare: order with four flavours, Milk, Dark, Hazelnut and Almond, 100 cartons each. Stock for Milk and Dark. Production order for Hazelnut due in 6 days. Rule and release rule as above.

    No.StepExpected result
    6.1Run the assignment variantMilk and Dark fixed to stock; Hazelnut reserved against the production order; Almond unassigned
    6.2Run the release checkOrder not released (50% ready, 90% needed)
    6.3Try to create a deliveryNo delivery for this order
    6.4Receive Hazelnut and Almond; rerun assignment and release checkAll fixed; order released; delivery can be created
    6.5Create a second, later order for Milk and run againIt does not take the stock fixed to the first order
    6.6In Adjust Supply Assignment, unassign one line by handStock is free again and visible in Supply Demand Overview
    6.7In Release for Delivery, move 50 from one due order to another and releaseBoth orders show the new confirmed quantities
    Troubleshooting

    Product ignored by the runNot marked relevant for supply assignment in that plantSet the field on the product
    Variant cannot be saved or runNo supply assignment rule enteredCreate and enter a rule
    Order assigned but never deliveredRelease check required but not run, or percentages not reachedRun the release check; review the rule
    Stock shows as free again after the delivery is createdThe delivery's checking rule does not respect the assignmentReview the scope of check for the delivery rule; see SAP KBA 3682445

    AATP · Chapter 7

    Supply Creation-Based Confirmation

    When stock and planned receipts are not enough, the system plans new production on the spot and confirms the order from that plan.

    Business scenario A corporate buyer orders 1,000 custom-printed gift boxes. Stock is 600. Nothing more is planned. The sales person wants to give a delivery date he can trust for the other 400 while the customer is still on the phone.

    The idea

    The availability check finds the gap. It then asks the production planning tool (PP/DS, the detailed scheduling part of S/4HANA) a real question: "Can you make 400, and by when?" PP/DS looks at free machine time and at components, and creates a planned order. The sales order is confirmed against that planned order.

    How it differs from replenishment lead time

    Replenishment lead time (Chapter 1)Supply creation-based confirmation
    What it isA fixed number of days on the product masterA real plan made at that moment
    Looks at capacity?NoYes
    Looks at components?NoYes
    Creates anything?No. It only assumes.Yes, a planned order
    How far to trust the dateLow when the factory is busyHigh

    Facts to remember

    • It arrived with the 2022 release. It replaces the older "capable-to-promise" function from SAP APO.
    • It needs two licences: AATP and PP/DS.
    • It is aimed mainly at make-to-order and assemble-to-order businesses, where each order drives production and capacity is the limit.
    • It must be activated in customising, and PP/DS must be set up for the product.
    Does a chocolate company need it? Usually not for the main business. Standard bars and gift boxes are made to stock from a forecast and sold from depots. The earlier chapters cover that. It becomes interesting for made-to-order lines such as corporate gifting or private-label orders.

    Go deeper: configuration

    Setup outline

    This function is mostly a production planning project. The sales consultant needs to know the outline and who to involve.

    No.AreaWhat is needed
    1LicenceAATP and PP/DS
    2AATP customisingActivate supply creation-based confirmation. Use a checking group with Advanced ATP active and the supply creation option set.
    3Check typeChoose one: the normal availability check followed by supply creation for the shortfall; or a production-planning-based check followed by supply creation
    4PP/DS customisingThe delivered heuristic SAP_PP_SBC is available and the strategy profile SAP_SBC is entered in the PP/DS global parameters
    5Master dataProduct is planned in PP/DS, with production version, resources with capacity, and components
    6TestOrder with a shortfall; a temporary planned order appears; on save it becomes a real planned order and the order is confirmed against it
    SymptomLikely causeFix
    Message that the check is not possibleProduct not set up for PP/DS, or activation incompleteCheck steps 2 to 5 with the PP consultant
    No planned order is createdHeuristic not triggeredCheck global parameters; see SAP KBA 3498199
    Date is far outNo free capacity or a component is missingThis is the real answer. Review capacity with planning.

    AATP · Chapter 8

    Putting it together

    How the parts combine on one order, which part answers which business problem, and how to run an AATP project.

    One order, all the checks

    Business scenario Diwali week. The Delhi depot has 10,000 festive gift boxes. 1,000 are protected for e-commerce. The North region has 3,000 left in this month's quota. A North general trade distributor orders 5,000.

    What can happen to the open 2,000:

    • If alternatives are allowed, the system tries another depot. The quota still applies there, so in this case it would not help.
    • If forward consumption is allowed, the system uses next month's North quota and confirms a date next month.
    • If neither, the 2,000 stay unconfirmed. A later backorder run will confirm them when quota or priority allows.

    Which part for which problem

    The business saysUse
    "Orders are confirmed but stock is never there."Availability check: review scope of check and replenishment lead time
    "One big customer takes everything."Product Allocation
    "This channel must always find stock."Supply Protection
    "Important orders that come late get nothing."Backorder Processing
    "Stock is in the next depot but the order shows short."Alternative-Based Confirmation
    "We ship half the festive range." / "Pre-booked orders lose their stock."Supply Assignment with release check
    "Dispatch needs to shift stock between orders at the last minute."Release for Delivery
    "We need a trustworthy date for made-to-order items."Supply Creation-Based Confirmation

    How to run an AATP project

    1. Licence and scope. Confirm the AATP licence. For supply assignment and supply creation, confirm those too.
    2. Pick the products. Start with the products that are often short. Give them a new checking group with AATP active.
    3. Fix the basics. Clean scope of check, lead times, routes and shipping point times. Advanced features cannot repair a wrong basic check.
    4. Get the priority rules in writing. Who is a key account? Which channel comes first? Who decides quotas each month? This is a business decision, not an SAP one.
    5. Build in this order: availability check, backorder processing, then allocation or protection, then alternatives. Each step is useful by itself.
    6. Simulate. Run backorder processing in simulation with real orders and walk through the monitor with the sales head.
    7. Name the owners. Someone must maintain quotas and protected quantities every cycle and read the backorder monitor every morning.
    8. Train the order desk to read Review Availability Check Result, so they can explain a confirmation to a customer.
    What goes wrong most often
    • Old quotas and protections left active after the shortage ends.
    • Rules too detailed for anyone to maintain.
    • Nobody tells customers when the backorder run takes their confirmation away.
    • Plant substitution switched on without checking GST and freight.
    • Old rescheduling jobs left running, doing nothing for AATP products.

    AATP · Always open

    Worked example: from zero to a tested order

    One complete build. Follow it in a sandbox system, in this order, and you will have used the availability check, a quota, protection and a backorder run together.

    The case

    Business scenario Cocoa Crest Chocolates sells the festive gift box GB-100 from its Delhi depot (plant 1000, sales organisation 1000). Diwali demand is far above supply. The sales head wants three rules: each region gets a fixed monthly share; e-commerce always finds 1,000 pieces a week; key modern trade accounts are served before everyone else, and blocked customers lose their stock.
    CustomerTypeChannelCustomer groupRegion
    D-NORTHDistributor10GTNorth
    D-SOUTHDistributor10GTSouth
    D-EASTDistributor10GTEast
    D-WESTDistributor10GTWest
    MT-01Modern trade key account20MTNorth
    EC-01E-commerce site30ECWest

    Starting stock of GB-100 in plant 1000: 10,000. No receipts planned.

    Part A. Build

    No.WhereEntries
    A1Define Availability Check Group (OVZ2)New group Z1 "AATP finished goods": TotalSales A, TotDlvReqs A, Block QtRq ticked, Advanced ATP Active
    A2Configure Scope of Availability Check (OVZ9)Z1 / A and Z1 / B: sales requirements, deliveries, released production orders and purchase orders included; "Check without RLT" ticked; supply protection option ticked
    A3Requirement class (OVZG) and schedule line category (VOV6)Availability, requirement transfer and product allocation ticked for the class and category your standard order uses
    A4Product GB-100, plant 1000, MRP 3Availability check = Z1
    A5Manage Characteristic CatalogsProduct Allocation catalog: Sales Organization, Region. Supply Protection catalog: Distribution Channel. Backorder Processing catalog: Customer Group, Sold-to Party, Requested Delivery Date, Creation Date.
    A6Activate Product Allocation (customising)Activate = Yes; check date = requested delivery date
    A7Configure Product AllocationObject PAL_GB100_REGION: unit PC, period Month, sales orders, no collective allocation, characteristics Sales Organization + Region
    A8Manage Product Allocation Planning DataThis month: 1000/North 3,000; 1000/South 3,000; 1000/West 2,000; 1000/East 2,000. Status restricted availability.
    A9Manage Product Allocation SequencesSequence SEQ_GB100: backward 0, forward 0; group 10; one constraint with PAL_GB100_REGION, rate 1.0, valid this month and next
    A10Assign Product to Product AllocationGB-100, plant 1000, valid this month and next. Then set the object to active.
    A11Manage Supply ProtectionObject SUP_GB100_ECOM: GB-100, plant 1000, period Week, consumption by requested delivery date, characteristic Distribution Channel; group priority 1, value 30, protected 1,000 this week. Activate.
    A12Configure BOP SegmentKEY_MT: Customer Group = MT, sort by requested date. BLOCKED: Sold-to Party = D-NORTH (in real life, use the credit status). ALL_OTHER: Customer Group is GT or EC, with exclusion Sold-to Party = D-NORTH, sort by requested date then creation date.
    A13Configure BOP VariantDIWALI_GB100: sales orders; availability check; Win = KEY_MT; Redistribute = ALL_OTHER; Lose = BLOCKED
    Why the exclusion in A12 Without it, D-NORTH's order would match both ALL_OTHER and BLOCKED. Design segments so that every order has one clear home.

    Part B. Test, in this exact order

    All orders ask for delivery this week, part deliveries allowed. Check each result in Review Availability Check Result before saving.

    No.OrderAskedExpectedWhy
    B1D-NORTH5,0003,000Availability 9,000 (10,000 less 1,000 protected). North quota 3,000. Lower wins.
    B2EC-01800800Uses 800 of the protection (200 left) and 800 of the West quota (1,200 left)
    B3D-SOUTH3,0003,000Stock and South quota both allow it
    B4D-EAST2,0002,000Stock and East quota both allow it
    B5D-WEST1,2001,000West quota has 1,200 left, but stock is the limit now: 10,000 less 8,800 confirmed = 1,200, less 200 still protected = 1,000
    B6MT-012,5000North quota was used up by D-NORTH. This is the problem the backorder run will solve.

    Checkpoint. Product Allocation Overview should show: North 3,000 of 3,000 used; South 3,000 of 3,000; East 2,000 of 2,000; West 1,800 of 2,000. The protection object should show 800 consumed.

    B7. The backorder run

    Run DIWALI_GB100 in simulation, check the monitor, then run it for real.

    OrderStrategyBeforeAfterWhy
    D-NORTHLose3,0000Gives up stock and North quota
    MT-01Win02,500Served first; North quota is free again
    EC-01Redistribute800800Nothing to change
    D-SOUTHRedistribute3,0003,000Already full
    D-EASTRedistribute2,0002,000Already full
    D-WESTRedistribute1,0001,200Stock is free now (500 after protection); West quota has 200 left; it gets the missing 200

    End state: 9,500 confirmed, 500 free, of which 200 are still held for e-commerce. North quota shows 2,500 of 3,000 used.

    Part C. What to show the client

    1. B1 on the result screen: one order, two checks, the lower result wins.
    2. B5: a customer inside his quota still limited by protected stock.
    3. B6 and B7 together: the key account that came late, and how the night run corrects it without anyone touching an order.
    4. The monitor after B7: who gained, who lost. Ask the sales head who will call D-NORTH.

    Part D. Try these changes yourself

    • Set forward consumption to 1 and repeat B1. What happens to the other 2,000, and on which date?
    • Move ALL_OTHER from Redistribute to Fill and rerun B7. What changes for D-WEST?
    • Let the protection week end and rerun the check for a general trade order.
    • Add a second depot with stock and an alternative strategy for customer group MT only.

    AATP · Always open

    Project kit

    What to ask the client, what to decide, how to cut over and what to tick off before go-live.

    Workshop questions for the client

    Today's situation
    • Which products are regularly short? In which months?
    • How do you decide today who gets short stock? Who makes that call?
    • How often are orders confirmed and then not delivered on the date? Do you measure it?
    • Do you run any rescheduling job today? Does anyone trust its result?
    • How do customers learn that a date has moved?
    Availability check
    • Should stock in quality inspection count as available? How often does it fail?
    • Should planned production count, or only released production orders?
    • Do you promise from a lead time when nothing is planned? Should you?
    • Are transit times per route and handling times per depot correct in the system?
    • Which customers accept part deliveries? Which insist on complete orders?
    • Is stock promised by depot, or by storage location inside the depot?
    Sharing rules: quota and protection
    • By what do you want to share: region, channel, customer group, single customers?
    • Is the rule "at most" for a group (quota) or "at least" for a group (protection)?
    • Monthly or weekly numbers? Who sets them, from which plan, and by which day?
    • May a group use quota it did not use last month? May it borrow from next month?
    • What should a customer outside all rules receive?
    • Do contracts with penalties exist for any channel? For what quantity and period?
    • When does the shortage end, and who switches the rules off?
    Priorities for the backorder run
    • Name the customer groups from most to least important. Is there a written list of key accounts?
    • Which orders must never lose a confirmation once given?
    • What happens to orders of credit-blocked customers?
    • Do stock transfers to depots rank above or below customer orders?
    • Inside one group, what decides: delivery date, order date, delivery priority?
    • When should the run happen, relative to planning, goods receipts and delivery creation?
    • Who reads the result each morning, and who informs customers who lost?
    Alternatives, assignment and release
    • Which depots may supply in place of which? For which customers?
    • Who pays extra freight? Is the GST difference between states handled in pricing and invoices?
    • Which products may replace which? Does the customer need to agree?
    • Do you pre-book orders before stock exists? Must their stock be held for them?
    • What share of an order must be ready before you ship it?
    • Does dispatch need to move stock between orders on the day? Who is allowed to?

    Design decisions to record

    DecisionOptionsHow to decide
    Which products go on AATPAll; only short products; by product groupStart with short products. Add more after the first month.
    Replenishment lead timeOn; offOff for anything that is often short
    Receipts that countReleased production orders only; plus firmed planned orders; plus purchase ordersCount only what planning stands behind
    Quota or protection or bothSee Chapter 3 tableListen for "at most" and "at least"
    Quota split and periodRegion, channel, customer group; week or monthThe coarsest split the business accepts
    Catch-all quotaNone; manual # line; system-madeManual # line unless every value is planned
    Consumption periods0 to n backward and forwardStart with 0 and 0; add only on request
    Check date for quota and protectionMaterial availability date; requested delivery dateThe date the business plans by. Use the same for both.
    Segments and strategiesSeven strategiesFew orders in Win; most in Redistribute; blocked in Lose
    Exception handlingStop product; stop run; fallback variantStop the product and use a fallback
    Run timesNightly; plus middayAfter planning and receipts, before delivery creation
    AlternativesOff; plant; product; both. Inline or sub-items.Only after GST, freight and master data are proven
    OwnersNamed peopleOne for quota numbers, one for the morning monitor, one for customer calls

    Cutover steps

    1. Transports. Move customising: checking group, scope of check, requirement class and schedule line settings, product allocation activation, item category entries.
    2. App content. Catalogs, allocation objects, sequences, protection objects, segments and variants are created in the apps. Check whether your release can transport or export them. If not, re-create them in production from a written sheet and have a second person check each one.
    3. Roles. Assign the business roles. Test that each named owner can open their apps.
    4. Stop the old jobs. Remove V_V2 and similar jobs for the products in scope.
    5. Load numbers. Upload quota planning data and protected quantities for the current and next periods. Nothing is carried over from old allocation data.
    6. Switch the products. Change the checking group on the products, by mass change, at a quiet time. Existing orders keep their old confirmations.
    7. First run in simulation. Run the backorder variant in simulation over all open orders. Review the monitor with the sales head.
    8. First real run. Run it for real. This brings all open orders under the new rules.
    9. Tell customers. Send the list of orders that lost confirmation to the people who will call customers.
    10. Schedule. Set up the recurring jobs.
    Fallback plan If results are wrong on day one, put the products back on the old checking group and stop the new jobs. Orders keep whatever confirmation they have. Product allocation activation itself cannot be reversed, so set all quota lines to unrestricted until the problem is fixed.

    Go-live checklist

    AreaCheck
    LicenceAATP licence confirmed in writing; PP/DS and fashion functions too, if used
    ScopeList of products and plants on AATP signed off
    BasicsScope of check reviewed for rule A and B; lead time decision made; routes and shipping point times checked
    Order setupRequirement class and schedule line category ticks verified for every order type in scope
    CatalogsAll needed fields present; unused fields removed
    QuotaObjects active; products assigned with end dates; numbers loaded for two periods; catch-all decided
    ProtectionObjects active; quantities agreed; review date in the calendar
    BackorderSegments do not overlap; variant simulated on real data; fallback variant set; jobs scheduled
    AlternativesInvoice with correct GST tested from every alternative plant; freight rule agreed
    Old jobsOld rescheduling jobs removed
    TestingEvery chapter's test script passed in the quality system; the worked example run end to end
    PeopleOwners named; order desk trained on the result screen; process for customer calls agreed
    FallbackSteps written and tried once in the quality system

    First two weeks after go-live

    • Read the backorder monitor every morning with the sales head.
    • Check quota usage twice a week. Lines at zero with stock sitting are a warning.
    • Count orders confirmed but not delivered on the date. It should fall.
    • Collect every "why did I get only this much?" question. Each is a training point or a rule to adjust.
    • Hold a review at the end of week two and adjust segments, numbers and run times.

    Glossary

    ATP quantity
    Stock plus expected receipts minus what is already promised.
    Checking group
    Field on the product that says how it is checked and whether AATP is on.
    Checking rule
    Comes from the transaction: A for sales orders, B for deliveries.
    Scope of check
    The tick-boxes that say which stock, receipts and issues count.
    Replenishment lead time
    Days to make or buy the product. If on, anything is treated as available after that many days.
    Material availability date
    The date stock must be ready in the plant so that the delivery date can be met.
    Characteristic
    An order field used in rules: region, channel, customer group and so on.
    Product allocation object
    The container for one quota plan.
    Backward and forward consumption
    Using quota from earlier or later periods.
    Supply protection object
    Holds protected quantities for a product in a plant.
    Segment
    A filtered, sorted group of orders in backorder processing.
    Variant
    The recipe for one backorder run: segments and their strategies.
    Confirmation strategy
    Win, Gain, Improve, Redistribute, Fill, Lose or Skip.
    Alternative control
    Decides which orders may use another plant or product.
    Substitution strategy
    Decides how the system chooses between alternatives.
    Supply assignment (ARun)
    A fixed link between one supply and one order line.
    Release check
    Tests whether enough of an order is assigned before a delivery is allowed.
    PP/DS
    Production Planning and Detailed Scheduling, the planning tool used by supply creation-based confirmation.

    Short names

    ShortFull
    ATP / AATPAvailable-to-Promise / Advanced Available-to-Promise
    PACProduct Availability Check
    PALProduct Allocation
    SUPSupply Protection
    BOPBackorder Processing
