    Intercompany · Chapter 0

    Start here: one group, two companies, one truck

    Intercompany means two legal companies of the same group trade with each other. The goods move once, but the law sees two sales. This course shows how SAP S/4HANA handles that with the newer "advanced" process.

    The business in this course

    We stay with Cocoa Crest Chocolates. To keep taxes, licences and profit separate, the group runs two legal companies:

    Cocoa Crest ManufacturingCocoa Crest Retail
    What it doesOwns the factory and makes the chocolateOwns the customers, takes orders and sends the customer invoice
    Company code10002000
    Sales organisation10002000
    Plants1000 (factory)2000 (Delhi depot) and 2090 (transit plant, explained in Chapter 1)
    PeopleArjun, factory dispatchRiya, order desk; Meera, accounts

    A company code is simply SAP's word for a legal company that keeps its own books.

    Two situations you will meet

    SituationStorySAP name
    A customer order that another company deliversBig Mart orders 1,000 gift boxes (GB-100) from Retail. Retail has none in Delhi. The factory of Manufacturing ships straight to Big Mart.Intercompany sales
    Filling your own depot from another companyRetail's Delhi depot needs 5,000 gift boxes before Diwali. It orders them from the factory of Manufacturing.Intercompany stock transfer

    Why one truck needs two sales

    In the first story, only one truck drives from the factory to Big Mart. But legally two things happen:

    1. Manufacturing sells 1,000 boxes to Retail at an internal price (the transfer price), say ₹380 a box.
    2. Retail sells the same 1,000 boxes to Big Mart at the customer price, say ₹500 a box.

    Each company needs its own invoice, its own stock and profit figures, and its own tax postings. The job of the intercompany process is to produce all of that from one customer order, without anyone typing things twice.

    Classic and advanced: what changed

    SAP has had an intercompany process for decades. It is now called the classic process. From release 2022, S/4HANA also has an advanced process. Both exist side by side. You choose per document type.

    QuestionClassicAdvanced
    Does the selling company have a purchase order for what it buys from the sister company?NoYes, created automatically
    Does the delivering company have a sales order for what it sells to the sister company?NoYes, created automatically
    How does the selling company get the supplier invoice?Through an electronic message (IDoc) that must be set up and watchedPosted automatically against the purchase order, like a normal supplier invoice
    Who owns the goods while they are on the truck?Not clearly shown in the booksShown clearly, using "valuated stock in transit" (Chapter 2)
    Can you see the whole chain on one screen?No, you read the document flow piece by pieceYes, in the Monitor Value Chains app (Chapter 6)
    Extra licence?NoNo
    Why auditors like the advanced process Every company in the chain has a complete, normal set of documents: an order, a goods movement and an invoice. Nothing is implied. Stock on the road always belongs to exactly one company, and the books show which one.

    Words used in this course

    WordPlain meaning
    Selling companyThe company the customer buys from. Here: Retail (2000).
    Delivering companyThe company whose plant ships the goods. Here: Manufacturing (1000).
    Receiving companyIn a stock transfer, the company whose plant receives the goods. Here: Retail (2000).
    Transfer priceThe internal price one group company charges another.
    Stock in transitGoods that have left one place and not yet reached the next. "Valuated" means they still carry a money value in someone's books.
    Transfer of controlThe moment ownership passes from one party to the next.
    Value chainThe full set of linked steps and documents for one intercompany order.
    VCMValue Chain Monitoring. The engine that creates the follow-on documents and postings for you, and shows their status.

    How this course is built

    • Chapters 1 to 3 follow a customer order: the documents, the goods, then the money.
    • Chapter 4 does the same for a stock transfer between the two companies.
    • Chapter 5 is the full setup: master data and customising.
    • Chapters 6 and 7 cover daily life: watching the chain, fixing errors, changes and limits.
    • Chapter 8 helps you decide and plan on a real project.

    The course is written against S/4HANA 2023 (on-premise and private cloud). Where later releases differ, it says so.

    Intercompany · Chapter 1

    Advanced intercompany sales: the documents

    Riya enters one normal sales order. The system builds the rest of the chain: a purchase order in her company and a sales order in the factory's company.

    Business scenario Big Mart orders 1,000 festive gift boxes GB-100 from Cocoa Crest Retail for delivery on 14 October. The Delhi depot is empty. The factory (plant 1000) of Cocoa Crest Manufacturing has 6,000 boxes. Riya wants the factory to ship directly to Big Mart.

    The idea

    Riya creates the order exactly as she always does. The only difference is the delivering plant on the item: plant 1000, which belongs to the other company. SAP sees that the plant's company (1000) is not the order's company (2000) and treats the item as intercompany.

    When she saves, the Value Chain Monitoring engine (VCM) does two things in the background, usually within seconds:

    1. It creates a purchase order in Retail: "Retail buys 1,000 GB-100 from Manufacturing".
    2. It creates an intercompany sales order in Manufacturing: "Manufacturing sells 1,000 GB-100 to Retail".

    These two are mirror images. Together with Riya's order they form the value chain.

    The documents, one by one

    No.DocumentCompanyWho creates itStandard type
    1Customer sales orderRetail (2000)RiyaOrder type OR, item category TAN
    2Intercompany purchase orderRetail (2000)SystemA purchase order type set up for this purpose (SAP delivers NBAI in recent releases)
    3Intercompany sales orderManufacturing (1000)SystemOrder type CBIC, item category CBIC, schedule line category CI
    4Outbound deliveryShipped from plant 1000Arjun, with reference to Riya's orderDelivery type LF
    5Goods movementsBothArjun posts goods issue; the system posts the restChapter 2
    6Intercompany invoiceManufacturing (1000) bills RetailBilling run or userBilling type IV2
    7Supplier invoiceRetail (2000)SystemPosted against the purchase order
    8Customer invoiceRetail (2000) bills Big MartBilling run or userBilling type F2

    Three things that surprise people

    • The delivery is created from Riya's order, not from the internal sales order. There is one delivery, one picking, one truck. The internal sales order (CBIC) exists for the books and for billing; nobody ships from it.
    • The internal sales order does not reserve stock. Its schedule line category CI has no availability check and creates no requirement. The requirement at the factory already comes from Riya's order, so reserving again would count the demand twice.
    • Nobody maintains the purchase order or the internal sales order by hand. They follow Riya's order. If she changes quantity or date, the system changes them (Chapter 7).

    The transit plant

    Retail never physically touches these boxes. But for a short time Retail owns them: after Manufacturing has sold them to Retail and before Big Mart takes them over. Stock in SAP must sit in a plant, so Retail needs a plant to own them in. That is the transit plant.

    In our example it is plant 2090. It is a plant that exists only in the system: no building, no people, no shelves. The purchase order receives the goods into 2090, and the goods leave to the customer from there, all by automatic postings. You see the transit plant on the sales order item, next to the delivering plant.

    Keep the transit plant simple Use a separate plant with one plain storage location. Do not manage it with a warehouse system (EWM) and do not switch on quality inspection for the product in that plant. The postings there are automatic and must never wait for a person.

    What Riya and Arjun see

    PersonSeesDoes
    Riya (Retail)Her order with delivering plant 1000 and transit plant 2090. In the document flow: the delivery and later her invoice. In Monitor Value Chains: the full chain.Enters and changes the order. Nothing else.
    Arjun (Manufacturing)A delivery due list with Riya's order in it, like any other order shipping from his plant.Creates the delivery, picks, posts goods issue.
    Meera (Retail accounts)A purchase order, later a supplier invoice posted against it.Normally nothing. She steps in only if the invoice is parked with an error.

    Go deeper

    App walkthrough: create the order and look at the chain

    1. Create the order. App: Manage Sales Orders, then Create Sales Order (or transaction VA01).

    FieldExample valueNote
    Order typeORMust be enabled for the advanced process (Chapter 5)
    Sales organisation / channel / division2000 / 10 / 00Retail's sales area
    Sold-to partyBig Mart
    Material, quantityGB-100, 1,000 boxes
    Requested delivery date14 October
    Plant (delivering plant)1000Type it, or let it come from the customer-material info record, the customer or the material master, as in any order
    Transit plant2090Proposed by the system from customising. Shown on the item, Shipping tab.

    The availability check runs in plant 1000 as usual. If Advanced ATP is active there, everything from the AATP course applies.

    2. Save. Note the order number, say 500. Wait a few seconds.

    3. Look at the chain. App: Monitor Value Chains. Search with the sales order number. Open the line and go to the Process Flow tab. You see the steps as boxes: purchase order created, intercompany sales order created, then the delivery and posting steps still open.

    4. Open the purchase order from the monitor. Check: supplier is the business partner that stands for plant 1000, plant is 2090, quantity 1,000, net price ₹380.

    5. Open the intercompany sales order. Check: type CBIC, sold-to party is the business partner that stands for Retail, plant 1000, price ₹380, schedule line category CI.

    6. Create the delivery. App: Create Outbound Deliveries - From Sales Orders (or VL10A / VL01N), shipping point of plant 1000, sales order 500. Pick and post goods issue. What happens next is Chapter 2.

    How the system decides an item is "advanced"

    All of these must be true for an order item:

    1. The delivering plant belongs to a different company code than the sales organisation.
    2. The order type is assigned to a value chain category for advanced intercompany sales.
    3. The item category is assigned too.
    4. The combination of order type and item category is enabled for the value chain.

    If the plant belongs to another company but the type or item category is not enabled, the item runs as classic intercompany. One order can hold classic and advanced items together. They cannot share one intercompany invoice.

    Customising path (details in Chapter 5):

    Sales and Distribution > Sales > Sales Documents > Integration with Value Chain Monitoring

    Intercompany · Chapter 2

    Who owns the goods on the truck

    Between the factory gate and the customer's door, the boxes change owner twice. Two dates on the delivery tell the system when.

    Business scenario Arjun posts goods issue for Big Mart's 1,000 boxes on 10 October. The truck needs three days. The group's rule is: Retail takes ownership the moment the truck leaves the factory. Big Mart takes ownership when it signs for the goods, on 13 October. On 11 October it is month-end for the auditors' test count. Whose stock are the 1,000 boxes?

    The idea

    The answer is Retail's. The advanced process can show this because it keeps goods on the road in valuated stock in transit: stock that is in no warehouse but still has a value in one company's books.

    The boxes pass through four states:

    StateOwnerWhat triggers the move into this state
    1. On the shelf in plant 1000Manufacturing
    2. In transit, still Manufacturing'sManufacturingArjun posts goods issue on the delivery
    3. In transit, now Retail'sRetailThe internal transfer of control date is reached
    4. Sold to Big MartBig Mart (no longer in our books)The external transfer of control date is reached

    The two dates

    DateMeaningIn our story
    Internal transfer of controlOwnership passes from the delivering company to the selling company10 October, when the truck leaves
    External transfer of controlOwnership passes from the selling company to the customer13 October, when Big Mart signs

    Both dates sit on the outbound delivery header, on the Shipment tab. Each exists twice: a planned date the system proposes, and an actual date you can enter when you know what really happened.

    A background job watches these dates. It posts the next goods movement when:

    • an actual date has been entered and is in the past, or
    • no actual date is entered, and the planned date plus a waiting time (the offset) is in the past.

    So if nobody does anything, the chain still completes on the planned dates. If the truck is late and you want the books to be exact, you enter the actual dates.

    What gets posted, in order

    StepPostingWhoEffect in the books
    AGoods issue on the deliveryArjunStock leaves the shelf of plant 1000 and enters Manufacturing's stock in transit. No sale yet. Manufacturing's stock value is unchanged.
    BGoods issue from Manufacturing's stock in transitSystem, on the internal dateManufacturing has now delivered to Retail. Its stock goes down and its cost of goods sold goes up.
    CGoods receipt for the purchase order in the transit plant. The stock is then held as Retail's stock in transitSystem, same moment as BRetail's stock goes up, valued at the purchase order price (₹380).
    DGoods issue from Retail's stock in transit to the customerSystem, on the external dateRetail has delivered to Big Mart. Its stock goes down and its cost of goods sold goes up.

    Arjun posts once. The system posts three times. Each posting creates a normal material document you can display.

    Answer to the scenario On 11 October, step B and C have happened (internal date 10 October) and step D has not (external date 13 October). The 1,000 boxes are in Retail's valuated stock in transit, worth ₹3,80,000 in Retail's books. Manufacturing no longer shows them.

    Why this matters to the business

    • Revenue at the right time. Each company shows its sale only when ownership has really passed.
    • Month-end is clean. Goods on the road are in exactly one company's stock. Nothing is counted twice or lost.
    • Contract terms can be followed. If the customer contract says ownership passes on arrival, the external date reflects that. If it passes at the factory gate, set both dates to the goods issue day.

    Go deeper

    App walkthrough: confirm the dates

    1. App: Manage Outbound Deliveries, or Change Outbound Delivery (VL02N). Open the delivery.

    2. Go to the header, Shipment tab. You see four fields:

    FieldExampleNote
    Planned internal transfer of control date10 OctoberProposed by the system
    Actual internal transfer of control date10 OctoberEnter when known
    Planned external transfer of control date13 OctoberProposed by the system
    Actual external transfer of control date13 OctoberEnter when the customer has taken over

    3. Save. At its next run the background job posts steps B and C, and later D.

    4. Check in Monitor Value Chains: the stock-in-transit steps turn green one after the other. Each shows its material document.

    If you use proof of delivery (the customer confirms receipt and you record it), confirming the proof of delivery can set the actual external date. Decide with the business who records arrival and how.

    The exact proposal logic for the planned dates, and the offset, depend on release and settings. Test it on your system with a delivery whose route takes several days.

    Movement types

    A movement type is the three-digit code that tells SAP what kind of stock posting this is. You will see these in the material documents of an advanced intercompany sale:

    StepMovement typeMeaning
    A687Transfer from the shelf to the delivering company's valuated stock in transit (reversal 688)
    B601Goods issue for delivery, taken from stock in transit
    C101Goods receipt for the purchase order, in the transit plant
    D601Goods issue for delivery to the customer, from the selling company's stock in transit

    The assignment of movement types to the process steps is delivered by SAP. Copy it from the delivery client; do not build it by hand. The stock transfer process in Chapter 4 uses a different set (681, 685, 107, 109).

    Where to look at stock in transit: Stock Overview (MMBE) or the app Stock - Single Material shows it as a special stock for the plant.

    Troubleshooting
    SymptomLikely causeFix
    Goods issue posted but nothing happens afterwardsThe dates are still in the future, or the background job is not scheduledCheck the dates on the delivery; check the job (Chapter 5)
    Step B or C fails with a posting period messageThe materials period or accounting period is closed in one of the two companies for that dateOpen the period or agree a posting date with finance, then reprocess
    Step C fails with a storage location or material messageGB-100 does not exist in the transit plant, or has no storage location or accounting view thereExtend the material to plant 2090 with all needed views, then reprocess
    Step fails with an authorisation messageThe background user is not allowed to post in that plantGive the technical user the missing authorisation (Chapter 5)
    Wrong date was confirmedUser errorCancel the step in Monitor Value Chains where allowed, correct the date, let it post again. Involve finance if the period has closed.

    Intercompany · Chapter 3

    The money: prices and three invoices

    One delivery produces three invoices: Manufacturing bills Retail, Retail books that bill as a purchase, and Retail bills the customer.

    Business scenario The 1,000 gift boxes have reached Big Mart. Big Mart pays ₹500 a box. The group has agreed that Manufacturing charges Retail ₹380 a box. It costs Manufacturing ₹300 to make one. Meera in Retail accounts wants the internal bill in her books without typing it, and the finance head wants to see what each company earned.

    The three invoices

    InvoiceFrom → toAmountCreatedStandard type
    Intercompany invoiceManufacturing → Retail1,000 × ₹380 = ₹3,80,000By the billing run in Manufacturing, from the deliveryIV2
    Supplier invoiceThe same bill, seen from Retail's side₹3,80,000Automatically, against the intercompany purchase orderSupplier invoice (invoice verification)
    Customer invoiceRetail → Big Mart1,000 × ₹500 = ₹5,00,000By the billing run in Retail, from the deliveryF2

    Taxes are added on top of each invoice according to your country's rules. They are left out here to keep the numbers easy.

    What each company earned

    ManufacturingRetailGroup
    Sells for₹380₹500₹500
    Cost₹300 (making it)₹380 (buying it)₹300
    Profit per box₹80₹120₹200

    The transfer price of ₹380 decides how the group's ₹200 is split between the two companies. That is why tax authorities care about it, and why finance, not sales, owns that number.

    Where each price comes from

    PriceDocumentMaintained asBy
    Customer price ₹500Riya's sales orderA normal sales price condition (standard condition type PPR0) in sales org 2000Retail sales
    Transfer price ₹380, buying sideIntercompany purchase orderA purchasing price for GB-100 from the supplier that stands for plant 1000: a purchasing info record or price condition (PMP0) in Retail's purchasing organisationRetail purchasing, with finance
    Transfer price ₹380, selling sideIntercompany sales order (CBIC) and invoice IV2A normal sales price condition (PPR0) in sales org 1000 for the customer that stands for RetailManufacturing sales, with finance
    The golden rule: both sides of the transfer price must match The purchase order says what Retail expects to pay. The intercompany invoice says what Manufacturing charges. The system checks one against the other when it posts the supplier invoice. If the purchase order says ₹380 and the invoice says ₹385, the supplier invoice does not post cleanly. Maintain the two prices together, with the same validity dates, every time.

    What is different from the classic process

    • Classic uses special intercompany condition types inside the customer's sales order (PI01, PI02) and in the intercompany invoice (IV01, IV02). The advanced process does not need them. Each document uses ordinary prices because each company now has its own ordinary order.
    • Classic sends the bill to the buying company as an electronic message (IDoc) that has to be mapped and monitored. Advanced posts a supplier invoice directly against the purchase order, with a three-way check of order, goods receipt and invoice, as for any outside supplier.
    • Classic uses billing type IV. Advanced uses IV2.

    The automatic supplier invoice

    When the intercompany invoice IV2 is posted to accounting in Manufacturing, the system creates the supplier invoice in Retail. It takes the quantities and amounts from IV2 and the reference from the purchase order.

    Three settings steer this (details in Chapter 5):

    • Tax code mapping. The sales tax code on the IV2 invoice has to be translated into a purchase tax code for the supplier invoice.
    • What to do on error. Usual choice: park the invoice. It is saved but not posted, and Meera gets it in her worklist to correct.
    • Posting date. Which date the supplier invoice uses, so both companies book in the same period.

    Order of billing

    Both invoices are created from the same delivery. An invoice can be created once the goods movement for its sale has been posted: the intercompany invoice after the internal transfer of control, the customer invoice after the goods issue to the customer. In daily work the normal billing due lists pick them up when they are ready; nobody needs to remember. Confirm the exact timing on your system in the first test.

    There is also a pro forma type, IV3, for a paper that looks like the intercompany invoice but posts nothing. It is used where a document must travel with the truck before the real invoice exists.

    Go deeper

    App walkthrough: bill and check

    1. Intercompany invoice. App: Create Billing Documents (or VF01 / VF04). Select the delivery. In the billing due list the delivery appears twice: once for sales org 1000 with billing type IV2, once for sales org 2000 with F2. Create IV2.

    Check on IV2Expected
    PayerThe customer that stands for Retail
    Net value₹3,80,000
    Accounting documentPosted in company code 1000

    2. Supplier invoice. Open Monitor Value Chains for order 500. The step for the supplier invoice turns green and shows the invoice number. Open it (app Supplier Invoices List, or MIR4). Check: company code 2000, reference to the purchase order, amount ₹3,80,000, status posted.

    3. Purchase order history. Open the purchase order. The history shows one goods receipt and one invoice receipt for 1,000 boxes. The clearing account for goods received and invoices received is balanced.

    4. Customer invoice. Create F2 for the same delivery. Net value ₹5,00,000 in company code 2000.

    5. Cancel, if you need to. Cancelling IV2 creates a cancellation document of type IV2S, and the system reverses the supplier invoice. Cancel in the reverse order of creation: invoices first, then goods movements.

    Price conditions with example values
    WhereTransaction / appKeyValueValid
    Customer priceManage Prices - Sales (VK11), PPR0Sales org 2000, customer Big Mart, material GB-100₹500 per box1 Oct to 31 Dec
    Transfer price, selling sideManage Prices - Sales (VK11), PPR0Sales org 1000, customer "Retail", material GB-100₹380 per box1 Oct to 31 Dec
    Transfer price, buying sidePurchasing info record (ME11) or Manage Prices - Purchasing (MEK1), PMP0Purchasing org 2000, supplier "plant 1000", material GB-100₹380 per box1 Oct to 31 Dec

    Notes:

    • The purchase order cannot be created without a price. A missing purchasing price is the most common reason the chain stops at the very first step.
    • Because the documents are created by the system, users are not meant to change the price inside the intercompany purchase order. Correct the price record, then let the chain re-price or reprocess.
    • Use the same unit of measure and the same currency on both sides. A price per box on one side and per carton on the other is a classic source of small differences.
    • Internal cost (condition PCIP) still shows each company's own cost in its own document, so margins can be read per company.

    SymptomLikely causeFix
    Supplier invoice is parked, not postedPrice or quantity differs from the purchase order, or the goods receipt (step C in Chapter 2) is not yet postedCompare the three: order, receipt, invoice. Correct the cause, then post the parked invoice.
    Supplier invoice step fails: tax code not determinedNo mapping from the sales tax code on IV2 to a purchase tax codeMaintain the tax code assignment (Chapter 5), then reprocess
    IV2 does not appear in the billing due listInternal transfer of control not yet posted, or copy control for IV2 missingCheck the chain in the monitor first, then copy control from delivery to IV2

    Intercompany · Chapter 4

    Advanced intercompany stock transfer

    No customer this time. Retail's depot orders stock from Manufacturing's factory. The chain starts from a purchase order instead of a sales order.

    Business scenario Diwali is five weeks away. Kabir, the planner for the Delhi depot (plant 2000, Retail), needs 5,000 gift boxes GB-100 on his shelves by 1 October. The factory (plant 1000, Manufacturing) will send them by road, two days away. The boxes become Retail's when the truck leaves the factory.

    The idea

    It is the same pattern as in Chapters 1 to 3, turned around. The leading document is now a purchase order that Kabir (or the planning run) creates in Retail. The system answers it with an intercompany sales order in Manufacturing. Then goods and invoices follow.

    No.StepCompanyWhoStandard type
    1Stock transport purchase order: 5,000 GB-100 for plant 2000, supplier = plant 1000RetailKabir, or converted from a planning proposalPurchase order type NBIC
    2Intercompany sales orderManufacturingSystemOrder type CBIC
    3Outbound delivery from plant 1000, created with reference to the purchase orderManufacturingArjunDelivery type NCC3
    4Goods issueManufacturingArjunMovement type 681: into Manufacturing's stock in transit
    5Transfer of controlBothSystem, by date685 out of Manufacturing's stock in transit; 107 into Retail's "goods receipt blocked stock"
    6Inbound delivery for plant 2000RetailSystemCreated automatically
    7Goods receipt when the truck arrivesRetailDelhi depot staff109: from blocked stock to normal stock
    8Intercompany invoiceManufacturingBilling runIV2
    9Supplier invoiceRetailSystemAgainst the purchase order

    What is the same, what is different

    Intercompany sales (Chapters 1 to 3)Intercompany stock transfer
    Leading documentCustomer sales order in the selling companyPurchase order in the receiving company
    Purchase orderCreated by the systemCreated by the planner or the planning run
    Intercompany sales order CBICCreated by the systemCreated by the system
    Delivery is created fromThe customer sales orderThe purchase order
    Receiving plantA transit plant; nobody touches the goods thereA real plant; staff receive and put away
    Transfer of control datesInternal and externalOne transfer between the two companies
    InvoicesIV2, supplier invoice, customer invoice F2IV2 and supplier invoice only

    Goods receipt blocked stock, in plain words

    When control passes while the truck is still driving, Retail already owns 5,000 boxes that are not yet in its building. SAP books them into a holding state called valuated goods receipt blocked stock: "ours, counted in our value, but not here yet and not usable". When the truck arrives and the depot staff post the goods receipt, the boxes move to normal stock and can be sold.

    For Kabir this means: after the transfer of control he can see 5,000 boxes are on the way and already Retail's property. He cannot promise them from the shelf until the goods receipt.

    Planning keeps working The purchase order is a normal planned receipt in plant 2000, and a normal requirement in plant 1000. Planning (MRP) in both plants sees it. The availability check for sales orders in Delhi can count it as an expected receipt, exactly as in the AATP course.

    Go deeper

    App walkthrough with example values

    1. Create the purchase order. App: Manage Purchase Orders, Create (or ME21N).

    FieldExampleNote
    Order typeNBICIntercompany stock transfer
    SupplierBusiness partner that stands for plant 1000Not the supplying plant field of a classic stock transport order; a real supplier number
    Purchasing org / group / company code2000 / 001 / 2000
    Material, quantity, plantGB-100, 5,000, plant 2000

    2. Save and check. In Monitor Value Chains, search with the purchase order number. The CBIC sales order step is green. Open it: sales org 1000, sold-to = Retail, 5,000 boxes at ₹380.

    3. Deliver. App: Create Outbound Deliveries - From Purchase Orders (or VL10B). Shipping point of plant 1000. A delivery of type NCC3 is created. Pick and post goods issue. Material document with movement type 681.

    4. Transfer of control. On the delivery header, check the transfer of control date. At its next run the job posts 685 and 107. The inbound delivery for plant 2000 appears.

    5. Receive. When the truck arrives: post goods receipt on the inbound delivery (app Change Inbound Delivery, or VL32N; or MIGO with movement 109). Stock is now unrestricted in plant 2000.

    6. Bill. Create Billing Documents for the delivery: IV2 for ₹19,00,000. The supplier invoice in company 2000 follows by itself.

    Technical objects of the stock transfer
    ObjectStandard value
    Purchase order typeNBIC
    Value chain categoryICST (intercompany stock transfer)
    Intercompany sales order typeCBIC
    Delivery type / delivery item categoryNCC3 / NCC3
    Schedule line category of the deliveryN3
    Movement types681 goods issue into issuing stock in transit; 685 goods issue out of issuing stock in transit; 107 goods receipt into valuated goods receipt blocked stock; 109 goods receipt out of blocked stock into the warehouse
    Billing typesIV2, cancellation IV2S, pro forma IV3

    The delivery type for the purchase order is found the same way as for classic stock transport orders: by the combination of purchase order type, supplying plant and receiving plant, in the stock transport order settings of purchasing. The shipping data for the supplying plant (customer for the receiving plant, sales area, shipping point) is needed too. See Chapter 5.

    Intercompany · Chapter 5

    Setting it up: master data and customising

    Most of the work is master data: each company must exist as a customer and as a supplier for the other. The customising mainly switches the process on for your document types.

    Business scenario Cocoa Crest has run the classic intercompany process for years. The finance head wants the advanced process live before the next financial year. You are asked to list everything that must be set up, in an order that a small team can follow.

    The setup in five blocks

    BlockWhatOwner
    1. OrganisationPlants, sales areas, purchasing organisations, the transit plant, and the links between themSD and MM consultants
    2. Master dataBusiness partners for the companies and plants, material views, pricesMaster data team, finance for prices
    3. Sales and purchasing customisingEnable order types and item categories; check the delivered intercompany typesSD and MM consultants
    4. Invoice customisingTax codes, error handling and posting date of the automatic supplier invoiceMM and finance consultants
    5. EngineBackground jobs, event links, technical userBasis team with the consultants

    Block 2 in plain words: who must know whom

    Business partnerRoleCreated inUsed in
    "Retail" as a customerCustomerManufacturing's company code 1000 and sales area 1000/10/00Sold-to party of the CBIC order; payer of invoice IV2
    "Plant 1000 / Manufacturing" as a supplierSupplierRetail's company code 2000 and purchasing organisation 2000Supplier of the intercompany purchase order; party of the supplier invoice
    "Plant 2000" as a customer (stock transfer only)Customer / ship-toManufacturing's sales areaShip-to party of the delivery to the Delhi depot

    The supplier must be linked to its plant (plant 1000) in the supplier's purchasing data, and the customer and supplier numbers should point at each other, so the system can find one from the other.

    The material GB-100 must exist everywhere it is touched:

    WhereViews needed
    Plant 1000Sales (for sales org 1000 and 2000), plant data, storage, accounting
    Transit plant 2090Purchasing, plant data with a storage location, accounting. No quality inspection.
    Plant 2000 (stock transfer)Purchasing, planning, storage, accounting
    A practical tip Build a one-page "intercompany master data checklist" per material and per company pair, and make it part of the process for creating new products. On live systems, nine out of ten stopped chains are caused by a missing view or a missing price, not by customising.

    Suggested order of work
    1. Organisation (block 1) in the development system.
    2. Engine (block 5), then run VCM_CHECK.
    3. Customising (blocks 3 and 4) for one order type only.
    4. Master data (block 2) for one material and one company pair.
    5. Run the test scripts of Chapters 1 to 4 end to end.
    6. Only then widen to more order types, materials and company pairs.

    Intercompany · Chapter 6

    Watching the chain and fixing errors

    The system does many steps on its own. One app shows every chain, where it stands, and what stopped it.

    Business scenario Monday morning. Riya saved 40 Big Mart orders on Friday evening. Arjun says three of them are missing from his delivery list. Meera says one supplier invoice is "stuck". Nobody knows where to look first.

    The idea

    Look in Monitor Value Chains. Each intercompany order is one line there, called a value chain. Each chain is a row of steps. Each step has a status. A red step tells you exactly which document could not be created or posted, and why.

    How to read a chain

    Status of a stepMeaningWhat to do
    Completed (green)Done. The step shows the document it created.Nothing
    Planned / waitingWaiting for something: a user action (delivery, goods issue) or a date (transfer of control)Nothing, unless it waits longer than expected
    In processRunning right nowRefresh in a minute
    Failed (red)The system tried and got an error messageRead the message, fix the cause, reprocess
    CancelledThe step was reversed on purposeNothing

    The exact status words differ a little between releases. The colours and the idea are the same.

    The three-move routine for a red step

    1. Read. Open the chain, go to the message log of the red step. The message is the same one you would get if you created that document by hand: "No net price", "Material not maintained in plant 2090", "Posting period not open".
    2. Fix the cause. Almost always master data or an open period. Fix it where it belongs. Never create the missing document by hand; the chain would not know about it.
    3. Reprocess. Select the step and choose Reprocess. The step runs again and turns green. The steps behind it then continue on their own.
    Answer to the scenario Filter the monitor for chains with errors, created since Friday. The three missing orders show a red step "create purchase order": the new flavour they contain has no purchasing price yet. Maintain the price, select the three chains, reprocess. Minutes later Arjun sees them. Meera's invoice shows as parked because the price was changed on one side only on Friday. Align the prices, then post the parked invoice.

    Who should watch it

    • Name one owner per company pair. In small companies it is one key user for everything.
    • Check errors every morning, and again before the daily billing run.
    • Before month-end, make sure no chain is stuck between goods issue and invoice. A stuck chain means stock or revenue in the wrong company at closing.

    Intercompany · Chapter 7

    Changes, cancellations, returns and limits

    Orders change. The chain follows the leading document. Know what follows automatically, what does not, and where the process ends.

    Business scenario Big Mart calls three times in one week. First: make it 1,200 boxes instead of 1,000. Second: ship from the Chennai factory of Manufacturing instead (plant 1100), it is closer to our new store. Third, after delivery: 50 boxes arrived crushed, we are sending them back.

    The rule

    You change only the leading document: the customer sales order in a sale, the purchase order in a stock transfer. The system carries the change into the other documents. You never edit the automatic purchase order or the intercompany sales order yourself.

    Change in Riya's orderWhat the system does
    Quantity 1,000 → 1,200Changes the purchase order and the intercompany sales order to 1,200
    Delivery date movedChanges the dates in both
    Item rejected (reason for rejection set)Rejects or closes the matching items in both
    New item addedAdds an item in both (or creates new documents)
    Delivering plant changed to another plant of a sister company (for example 1000 → 1100)The old purchase order item and intercompany sales order item are rejected, and a new pair is created for the new plant. The purchase order is addressed to the supplier that stands for one plant, so a new plant needs a new one.
    Delivering plant changed to Retail's own plantThe old pair is rejected. The item is now a normal sale; no new chain.

    Changes are possible as long as the step they touch has not happened. Once a delivery exists, quantity changes are limited by the delivery, as in any sales order. Once goods have moved, you reverse steps from the end backwards.

    Undoing things: last in, first out

    To undoDoThe system then
    Customer invoiceCancel F2Normal cancellation
    Intercompany invoiceCancel IV2 (creates IV2S)Reverses the supplier invoice in Retail
    Transfer of control postingsCancel the step in Monitor Value ChainsReverses the material documents
    Goods issueReverse goods issue on the delivery (VL09)Stock returns to the shelf in plant 1000
    The orderReject the item in the leading documentRejects the items in the automatic documents

    Always undo in this order, top to bottom. You cannot reverse a goods issue while its invoice still stands.

    Returns

    For the 50 crushed boxes: in the releases this course describes, customer returns are not part of the advanced intercompany sales process. You handle them with the classic approach.

    • If the boxes go back to Retail's own depot: a normal returns order in Retail, credit memo to Big Mart. Nothing intercompany.
    • If the boxes go back to Manufacturing's factory: a returns order in Retail with the receiving plant 1000, processed as a classic intercompany return, with a credit from Manufacturing to Retail.

    Agree the returns route in the design workshop. Many groups decide that all customer returns go to the selling company's own depot, which keeps them simple.

    What is supported, and what is not

    Works in the advanced process (release 2023)Check the restriction note before promising
    Standard items sold from stock (TAN)Customer returns (run as classic)
    Free-of-charge items (CBXN)Third-party items and other special item types
    Batches and serial numbersMake-to-order and configurable products (added in later releases and cloud scope items)
    Classic and advanced items in the same sales orderWarehouse-managed (EWM) or quality-inspected transit plants: avoid
    Advanced ATP in the delivering plantChains with more than two companies (see below)

    One thing that is never possible: a classic item and an advanced item in the same intercompany invoice. They are billed with different billing types.

    More than two companies: multistage

    Some groups route a sale through a middle company. Example: a factory company in India sells to a regional trading company in Singapore, which sells to the retail company in Australia, which sells to the customer. Goods move once; three sales happen.

    From S/4HANA 2025 FPS01, the advanced process supports this as multistage intercompany sales and stock transfer. The principle is unchanged: every company in the chain gets its purchase order, its sales order (CBIC), its stock in transit and its invoices. The middle companies are described in a "financial chain" that you maintain with apps, and separate value chain categories exist for multistage sales and multistage stock transfer.

    On earlier releases, the advanced process handles exactly two companies.

    Go deeper

    Intercompany · Chapter 8

    Putting it together: decide, design, go live

    You now know the parts. This chapter helps you advise a client: classic or advanced, what to decide, and how to switch without stopping the business.

    Business scenario The finance head of Cocoa Crest asks you three questions in one meeting. Should we move to the advanced process at all? What do my teams have to decide? And how do we switch while hundreds of classic orders are still open?

    The whole picture on one page

    Question 1: classic or advanced?

    If the client says…Lean towardsWhy
    "Auditors ask who owns goods in transit at month-end."AdvancedValuated stock in transit answers it exactly
    "Our intercompany IDocs fail every week."AdvancedNo IDocs; the supplier invoice posts directly
    "Purchasing wants a real purchase order for what we buy from the sister company."AdvancedIt creates one
    "We want group reporting and profit elimination per value chain."AdvancedIt is the base SAP builds on for group valuation
    "We are on a release before 2022."ClassicAdvanced does not exist there
    "Our process depends on something in the restriction note."Classic for those items, advanced for the restBoth can run side by side
    "We are starting a new implementation now."AdvancedIt is where SAP invests

    Question 2: what must the client decide?

    DecisionOptionsWho decides
    Which company pairs and which order types go advanced firstAll at once, or one pair and one type as a pilotProject lead with finance
    Transfer price: where it is kept and who owns itInfo record and sales price maintained together by one teamFinance
    When control passes between the companiesAt goods issue, or on arrivalFinance and tax
    When control passes to the customerAt goods issue, on arrival, or on proof of deliverySales and finance, from the customer contracts
    Who confirms actual datesNobody (planned dates rule), dispatch, or customer serviceOperations
    Transit plantOne per selling company (usual), system-only plantConsultants
    What happens to a faulty supplier invoicePark it (usual) and who clears the parked listAccounts payable
    Who watches the monitorNamed key user per company pair, with a stand-inOperations
    Returns routeTo the selling company's depot, or classic intercompany returnSales and logistics

    Question 3: how to switch

    1. Open classic documents finish as classic. An order that started classic is delivered and billed classic. Do not try to convert open documents.
    2. Switch per order type. The process is enabled per order type and item category. Enable the pilot order type on the cutover date. New orders of that type run advanced from that moment.
    3. Keep classic working. Classic customising and its IDoc setup stay until the last classic order is billed, and for returns.
    4. Prepare master data before the switch. Business partners, material views in the transit plant and both prices must be loaded and checked first.
    5. Hold a short "hyper-care" on the monitor. For the first two weeks, look at failed chains twice a day.
    What to tell users on day one Riya: "Nothing changes for you, except a new field, transit plant, that fills itself." Arjun: "Same delivery, same goods issue." Meera: "You will see real purchase orders and supplier invoices from our sister company. Look at your parked invoices daily." Everyone: "If something is missing, open Monitor Value Chains before you call anyone."

    Month-end checklist

    • No chain in error in Monitor Value Chains for the closing period.
    • No delivery with goods issue posted but transfer of control overdue.
    • No parked intercompany supplier invoices.
    • Intercompany invoices (IV2) and supplier invoices agree in number and amount between the two companies.
    • Stock in transit per company reviewed and explained.

    Project kit

    Material you can take into a client project: workshop questions, design decisions, cutover steps and a go-live checklist.

    Workshop questions for the client

    Business and legal

    1. Which legal companies trade goods with each other? Draw every pair and the direction.
    2. For each pair: do goods go direct to the customer, into the other company's depot, or both?
    3. Is any sale routed through a third group company on paper?
    4. Who sets the transfer price? How often does it change? Is it cost plus a percentage, or a price list?
    5. What do your contracts and Incoterms say about when ownership passes to the customer?
    6. When should ownership pass between the group companies? Has tax advice been taken?
    7. What do auditors ask about goods in transit today?

    Operations

    1. How many intercompany order lines per day? Any peaks?
    2. Who creates deliveries for intercompany orders today, and from which list?
    3. Do you record proof of delivery? Who could confirm actual arrival dates?
    4. Are batches, serial numbers or shelf-life dates used?
    5. Is any plant involved managed by a warehouse system?
    6. How are customer returns of intercompany sales handled?
    7. Which special cases exist: free samples, third-party, made-to-order, consignment?

    Finance and systems

    1. How does the buying company receive the intercompany invoice today? What goes wrong?
    2. Which tax codes apply on each side, per company pair?
    3. Do both companies close their periods on the same day?
    4. Which release are you on, and which is planned?
    5. Do you use own order types and item categories? Which ones carry intercompany business?

    Design decisions to record

    No.DecisionRecommended default
    1Scope of the first go-liveOne company pair, one order type, stock items only
    2Transit plantOne system-only plant per selling company, one storage location, no warehouse management, no quality inspection
    3Internal transfer of controlAt goods issue, unless tax advice says otherwise
    4External transfer of controlFollows the customer contract; planned dates by default, actual dates entered only for exceptions
    5Transfer price maintenanceOne owner in finance maintains both sides in one work step, same validity
    6Supplier invoice on errorPark; accounts payable clears the list daily
    7Posting date of the supplier invoiceSame as the intercompany invoice
    8MonitoringNamed owner and stand-in; daily check; check before billing run and before closing
    9ReturnsTo the selling company's own depot
    10Classic processStays for open documents, returns and unsupported cases

    Roles and authorisations

    PersonNeeds
    Order desk (selling company)Sales orders in own sales org; display of the chain
    Dispatch (delivering company)Deliveries and goods issue in own plant; change of transfer of control dates if they confirm them
    Accounts payable (buying company)Parked supplier invoices
    Billing clerksIV2 in the delivering company, F2 in the selling company
    Key userMonitor Value Chains with reprocess and cancel
    Technical userCreate and change all automatic documents in all companies involved

    Cutover steps

    WhenStep
    4 weeks beforeMaster data load plan agreed: business partners, material views for transit plants, both prices. Trial load in the test system.
    2 weeks beforeFull end-to-end test with real materials and real prices, including month-end and one reversal
    1 week beforeCustomising and jobs transported to production with the process still switched off (order types not yet enabled). Run VCM_CHECK in production.
    3 days beforeLoad master data in production. Check ten materials by hand in every plant.
    Cutover dayEnable the order type and item category. Create one real order and follow it to the purchase order and intercompany sales order.
    Day 1 to 14Monitor twice daily. Daily ten-minute call: errors found, cause, fix, prevention.
    First month-endRun the month-end checklist of Chapter 8 together with finance

    Go-live checklist

    • ☐ Restriction note for the release read; unsupported cases listed and routed to classic
    • ☐ Organisation settings complete for every company pair
    • ☐ Internal customers and suppliers created, linked, with trading partner
    • ☐ Materials extended to transit plants with accounting view
    • ☐ Purchasing price and internal sales price equal, same validity, same unit and currency
    • ☐ Order types and item categories enabled as planned, and only those
    • ☐ Tax code mapping maintained for every pair
    • ☐ Technical jobs scheduled; event links active; VCM_CHECK clean
    • ☐ Technical user authorised in all plants and companies
    • ☐ Monitoring owner named, trained, with a stand-in
    • ☐ Accounts payable knows the parked invoice list
    • ☐ Month-end checklist agreed with finance
    • ☐ Users briefed: what changes for each role

    Settlement · Chapter 0

    Start here: money you settle later

    Some deals cannot be put on the invoice, because the final amount is only known later. Settlement Management records such deals and pays them out at the agreed time.

    The business problem

    Cocoa Crest Chocolates tells its distributor Sharma Distributors: "If you buy more than ₹50 lakh from us this financial year, we give you back 2% of everything you bought. If you cross ₹1 crore, 3%."

    In April nobody knows how much Sharma will buy by next March. So the 2% or 3% cannot be a discount on each invoice. It is a rebate: money given back afterwards, once the result is known.

    Three questions follow, and every chapter of this course answers one of them:

    1. What was agreed? With whom, for which products, for which period, at which rates.
    2. How much has the customer bought so far? This figure is called the business volume.
    3. How much do we owe, and when do we pay it? Paying is called settlement. Putting money aside in the books until then is called accrual.

    The tool: the condition contract

    In S/4HANA the agreement is stored in a condition contract. It is one document that holds the partner, the validity dates, which sales count, the rates, and a calendar of settlement dates. The part of S/4HANA that manages these contracts is called Condition Contract Management, and it belongs to Settlement Management.

    What it replaced

    Older SAP systems (ECC) used "rebate agreements" in Sales. In S/4HANA you cannot create new ones. Existing old agreements may run until they end; everything new is a condition contract.

    QuestionOld rebate agreementCondition contract
    Agreement made in June for sales since April?Needed a heavy rebuild program for old invoicesWorks directly. Sales are read from the invoices at settlement time.
    Where is the running total kept?In a special statistics table that often got out of stepNowhere special. It is calculated from the invoices whenever needed.
    Who can be the partner?Customers onlyCustomers and suppliers, with one common tool
    What can be settled?Sales rebatesSales rebates, purchase rebates, commissions, royalties and similar
    Settlement datesRun by handA calendar in the contract; a job settles what is due

    Where else it is used

    DealExample at Cocoa CrestMoney flows
    Sales rebate2% back to Sharma Distributors on yearly purchasesWe pay the customer
    Purchase rebateThe cocoa supplier gives 1.5% back if we buy over 500 tonnesThe supplier pays us
    CommissionAn outside sales agent earns 1% on orders he bringsWe pay the agent
    RoyaltyWe pay a cartoon brand ₹4 for every box that carries its characterWe pay the licence owner

    This course teaches the sales rebate in depth (Chapters 1 to 5), then shows how the other deals differ (Chapter 6).

    Words used in this course

    WordPlain meaning
    RebateMoney given back to a customer after the sale, based on how much was bought
    Condition contractThe document that stores the deal
    Business volumeThe total of the sales that count for the deal
    AccrualAn amount set aside in the books now for a rebate that will be paid later
    SettlementWorking out the amount owed and creating the credit note
    Settlement documentThe document the system creates at settlement; it posts the credit to the customer's account
    ScaleSteps in the rate: 2% from ₹50 lakh, 3% from ₹1 crore

    Where this sits in the SAP process This chapter covers steps 1 to 12 of the end-to-end flow. Open the process flow in SAP.

    Settlement · Chapter 1

    The condition contract

    One document holds the whole deal. Learn its five parts and you can read any contract.

    Business scenario On 1 April the sales head signs the yearly deal with Sharma Distributors: 2% back on all chocolate bought between 1 April and 31 March if he reaches ₹50 lakh, 3% from ₹1 crore. Gift boxes sold at Diwali special prices do not count. Rebate is paid every quarter, with a final calculation after year-end. Priya, the sales administrator, must enter this.

    The five parts of a contract

    PartQuestion it answersSharma's contract
    1. HeaderWho, what kind of deal, from when to when?Type: sales rebate. Customer: Sharma Distributors. Valid 1 April to 31 March.
    2. Business volume selectionWhich sales count?All invoices to Sharma in sales organisation 1000, except material group "Diwali gift boxes"
    3. ConditionsWhat rate, with which steps?Rebate: 2% from ₹50,00,000; 3% from ₹1,00,00,000. Accrual: 2%.
    4. Settlement dataHow is it paid?As a credit to Sharma's account, in rupees
    5. Settlement calendarWhen?Partial settlement on 30 June, 30 September, 31 December. Final settlement on 31 March.

    The contract type decides the behaviour

    When Priya creates a contract she first picks a contract type. It works like an order type in sales: it sets the rules so that she only fills in the deal. SAP delivers ready types.

    TypeUse
    0S01Sales rebate for one customer
    0S02Sales rebate for several customers together, for example all outlets of a buying group
    Further typesVariants with different tax handling, supplier rebates, commissions, royalties (Chapter 6)

    Two different condition lines

    The Conditions part normally holds two lines. People mix them up, so keep them apart:

    LineStandard condition typePurposeSharma
    Rebate (settlement) conditionRES1What we really pay at settlement. May have scales.2% from ₹50 lakh, 3% from ₹1 crore
    Accrual conditionREA1What we set aside in the books on each invoice, as our best guess. No scale needed.2%

    The accrual rate is an estimate chosen by finance. It can differ from the rebate rate. Chapter 3 explains why.

    Status: a contract must be released

    A contract can be saved while the deal is still being discussed. It only takes part in accruals and settlement when it is released. A released contract can be locked again for settlement if a dispute comes up, without deleting anything. Companies that want a second pair of eyes switch on an approval workflow, so a manager releases what the administrator entered.

    Late start is fine The deal was signed on 1 April but Priya enters it on 20 May. She still sets "valid from 1 April". Because sales are read from the invoices when needed, April and May invoices count without any repair program. This is one of the biggest practical gains over the old rebate agreements.

    Settlement · Chapter 2

    Business volume: which sales count

    The rebate is a percentage of something. That something is the business volume. Get its definition right and most rebate disputes disappear.

    Business scenario In October Mr Sharma phones: "By my books I have crossed ₹50 lakh. Your statement says ₹46 lakh." Priya must explain the difference in minutes, invoice by invoice.

    The idea

    The system does not keep a running counter. Whenever the business volume is needed, it looks at the billing documents (invoices, credit memos, cancellations) and adds up those that match the contract:

    1. The invoice date lies inside the contract's validity.
    2. The invoice matches the "include" lines of the business volume selection, for example customer = Sharma.
    3. The invoice item does not match an "exclude" line, for example material group = Diwali gift boxes.

    Credit memos and cancelled invoices reduce the total automatically, because they are billing documents too.

    Answer to the scenario

    LineAmount
    All invoices to Sharma, April to October₹52,00,000
    Less: Diwali gift boxes (excluded in the contract)− ₹4,50,000
    Less: credit memo for damaged goods in August− ₹1,50,000
    Business volume₹46,00,000

    Priya opens the business volume display for the contract, which lists exactly these documents, and sends Mr Sharma the list.

    Which amount is added up

    Usually the net value of the invoice item, before tax. The business can agree something else: value after certain discounts, quantity in cartons, or weight in kilograms ("₹5 back for every carton"). Which amount or quantity is used is a setting in the business volume profile and the condition.

    Scales: the rate depends on the total

    Business volume on the settlement dateRateRebate
    ₹46,00,0000% (below the first step)₹0
    ₹60,00,0002%₹1,20,000
    ₹1,20,00,0003%₹3,60,000

    In the standard scale, once a step is reached the rate applies to the whole volume, not only the part above the step. If the business wants "2% on the first crore and 3% only on the rest", that is a graduated scale and must be chosen on purpose in the condition type.

    Write the definition into the deal letter "Net sales" means different things to different people. Agree in writing: before or after tax, before or after cash discount, are returns deducted, are promotional items included, which invoice date counts. Then build the selection to match the letter exactly.

    Go deeper

    Level of detailTotals, or every billing document item

    The result shows each billing document, its date, material, net value and whether it is already included in a settlement. Export it to a spreadsheet for the customer.

    Settlement · Chapter 3

    Accruals: setting money aside

    A rebate promised today is a cost today, even if it is paid next year. Accruals put that cost into the books month by month.

    Business scenario In June the finance head looks at the profit of the first quarter. Sales to Sharma were ₹30 lakh. No rebate has been paid. She asks: "Is the ₹60,000 we will probably owe him already in my figures, or will it hit me as a surprise in March?"

    The idea

    With accruals, it is already in her figures. Each time an invoice to Sharma is posted, the system also books a small entry: "2% of this invoice is a rebate cost, and we owe it to someone later." The customer does not see this entry. His invoice amount is unchanged.

    Invoice to SharmaCustomer paysHidden accrual booking (2%)
    ₹1,00,000 of chocolate bars₹1,00,000 plus taxRebate cost ₹2,000; rebate owed ₹2,000

    By the end of June: sales ₹30,00,000, accruals ₹60,000. The profit report already carries the cost. When the rebate is finally paid, the accrual is released and the real amount is booked. Only the difference between estimate and reality moves the profit at that time.

    Two ways to build accruals

    On each invoiceDelta accruals run
    HowThe accrual condition (REA1) is found during invoice pricing and posted with the invoiceA periodic run looks at the business volume, works out what should have been accrued, and posts the missing amount
    WhenImmediately, invoice by invoiceOn the dates of the "delta accruals" calendar, for example every month-end
    Good forNormal business, contract exists before invoicingContracts entered late; rate changes; businesses that do not want accrual lines in invoices
    NeedsThe accrual condition in the sales pricing procedureDelta accrual dates in the settlement calendar and the run scheduled

    Many companies use both: accruals on the invoice, plus a monthly delta run as a safety net. The delta run never double counts. It compares "should be" with "already accrued" and posts only the gap.

    Why the accrual rate may differ from the rebate rate

    Sharma's deal pays 0%, 2% or 3% depending on where he ends. Finance must choose one estimate for the year. If they expect him to land between ₹50 lakh and ₹1 crore, they accrue 2%. If by December he is clearly heading for ₹1.2 crore, they change the accrual condition to 3% and the next delta accruals run tops up the earlier months.

    Answer to the scenario Yes. ₹60,000 is already booked as cost in the first quarter and sits on an accrual account as "owed". Paying Sharma later will not hit the profit again, except for any difference between the 2% estimate and the final rate.

    Go deeper

    What the accounting entries look like
    EventDebitCreditAmount
    Invoice ₹1,00,000CustomerSales revenue₹1,00,000
    Accrual on that invoiceRebate expense (or sales deduction)Rebate accruals (a liability account)₹2,000
    Settlement of ₹2,000Rebate accrualsRebate expense₹2,000 (accrual reversed)
    Rebate expenseCustomer₹2,000 (real rebate credited)

    The accounts come from revenue account determination (transaction VKOA) through account keys on the condition types. The delivered keys are 0S1 for the rebate and 0S2 for accruals. Agree the accounts with finance; some companies show rebates as a reduction of revenue, others as an expense.

    Setup for accruals on the invoice
    1. Condition type REA1 exists with its access sequence. The access reads the condition contract conditions, so a contract must be found for the invoice.
    2. REA1 is placed in the sales pricing procedure that the invoice uses, near the end, marked statistical, with the accrual account keys.
    3. The contract contains an REA1 line and is released.

    Logistics - General > Settlement Management > Basic Settings > Pricing > Sales (SD)

    Test: create an invoice for Sharma. In the item conditions you see REA1 with 2%, statistical. In the accounting document you see the two accrual lines.

    Settlement date typeDelta accruals

    Settlement · Chapter 4

    Settlement: paying what is owed

    On each date in the calendar the system adds up the sales, applies the rate, takes off what was already paid, and credits the customer.

    Business scenario Sharma's year: ₹30 lakh in the first quarter, ₹60 lakh by end of September, ₹90 lakh by end of December, ₹1.2 crore by 31 March. His deal: 2% from ₹50 lakh, 3% from ₹1 crore, paid quarterly, final calculation at year-end. What does he receive, and when?

    Four kinds of settlement date

    KindWhat it doesTypical use
    Partial settlementPays what is earned so far. It is an advance: the same period is looked at again later.Quarterly or monthly payouts
    Final settlementCalculates the whole period once more with the final total, takes off the partial payments, and closes the periodYear-end, or end of the contract
    Delta settlementCorrects a period after its final settlement, because a late invoice or credit memo changed the totalLate corrections
    Delta accrualsPosts missing accruals only. Pays nothing.Month-end (Chapter 3)

    Sharma's year, step by step

    Every settlement starts from the contract's start date and looks at the total so far.

    DateKindVolume so farRate reachedRebate earned so farAlready paidCredit now
    30 JunePartial₹30,00,0000%₹0₹0₹0
    30 SeptemberPartial₹60,00,0002%₹1,20,000₹0₹1,20,000
    31 DecemberPartial₹90,00,0002%₹1,80,000₹1,20,000₹60,000
    31 MarchFinal₹1,20,00,0003%₹3,60,000₹1,80,000₹1,80,000

    Sharma receives three credits: ₹1,20,000, ₹60,000 and ₹1,80,000. Total ₹3,60,000, which is 3% of ₹1.2 crore. The final settlement lifted the earlier quarters from 2% to 3% by itself.

    What a settlement run produces

    1. A settlement document. It lists the business volume, the rate, the rebate amount and what is taken off.
    2. A credit on the customer's account in accounting. It reduces what Sharma owes on his next payment, or is paid out.
    3. The reversal of accruals for the settled amount (Chapter 3).
    4. A printed or e-mailed credit note for the customer, with tax where the law requires it.

    Nobody types an amount. If the amount looks wrong, the cause is in the contract or the invoices, never in the settlement document.

    Running it

    A scheduled job runs the settlement program every night for "all released contracts with a date due". The calendar in each contract decides what happens. Users run it by hand only for a single contract, or as a check run to see the result before it posts.

    Check run first The settlement program has a check mode that calculates everything and posts nothing. Use it before every important final settlement. Send the result to the sales head. Then run live.

    In India the credit note for a rebate has GST consequences that depend on how the deal is worded and timed. Decide the tax treatment with the client's tax adviser before choosing the contract type variant.

    Setting it up

    SAP delivers a working sales rebate. The setup is mostly: check what is delivered, copy it to your own keys, connect it to your pricing and your accounts.

    Business scenario Cocoa Crest goes live on S/4HANA in April. It has 140 distributor rebate deals. You must make the standard sales rebate work for sales organisation 1000 and hand over a list of what was configured.

    2. Contract maintenanceContract types and what may be entered in themSmall. Copy the delivered type.
    3. Contract settlementWhere sales are read from, settlement document types, calendars, accountsMedium. Accounts and tax need finance.

    Settlement · Chapter 6

    Other kinds of deals

    The same contract, volume, accrual and settlement logic serves groups of customers, suppliers, agents and licence owners. Only the partner, the source of the figures and the direction of the money change.

    Business scenario After the distributor rebates go live, four more requests arrive. Big Mart wants one rebate across its 60 stores. Purchasing wants to track the cocoa supplier's volume bonus. The sales head wants to pay an outside agent 1% commission. Legal reminds everyone of the ₹4-per-box royalty to a cartoon brand.

    One pattern, five deals

    DealPartner in the contractBusiness volume comes fromSettlement createsAccrual means
    Sales rebate, one customerThe customerOur invoices to himCredit to the customerCost set aside
    Sales rebate, several customersA list of eligible customers; one or each receives the creditOur invoices to all of themCredit to the owner, or split to eachCost set aside
    Purchase rebateThe supplierSupplier invoices or goods receipts for our purchasesA claim on the supplier (he pays us or we deduct it)Income expected
    CommissionThe agent (set up as a supplier)Our invoices for the customers or orders he looks afterA payable to the agentCost set aside
    RoyaltyThe licence owner (a supplier)Our invoices for the licensed products, usually by quantityA payable to the licence ownerCost set aside

    Several customers in one contract

    Big Mart's head office negotiates; 60 stores buy, each with its own customer number. Use the contract type for multiple customers (0S02). The head office is the contract owner. The stores are listed as eligible partners. The business volume is the total of all stores, so the scale is reached together. At settlement you choose: one credit to the head office, or a credit per store in proportion to its purchases.

    If the stores already hang under the head office in a customer hierarchy, you can select by hierarchy node instead of listing them, and new stores join by themselves.

    Supplier side

    The contract is created with the app for supplier contracts and settled with the supplier settlement program (transaction WB2R_SV). Volume is read from purchasing documents. The result is money we receive, so the accrual is expected income, and the settlement document is a debit to the supplier. Purchasing owns these contracts; the logic you learned is the same.

    Commission and royalty

    The partner is paid, like a customer rebate, but he is not the one who bought. So the contract separates two things: who gets paid (the agent, as contract partner) and whose sales count (the business volume selection: customers of his territory, or orders where he is entered as a partner). Royalties are usually a fixed amount per unit sold, so the condition is an amount per box and the business volume is a quantity.

    Advice for projects Go live with one deal type, normally the sales rebate. Add the others in later waves. Each uses its own delivered contract types and scope item, and each involves a different department: sales, purchasing, or legal.

    Go deeper

    Delivered contract types and tools by deal
    DealDelivered contract types (examples)Maintenance appSettlement
    Sales rebate, one customer0S01 (tax as for a service), 0SG1 (goods-related tax)Manage Condition Contracts - CustomersWB2R_SC
    Sales rebate, several customers0S02, 0SG2sameWB2R_SC
    Purchase rebateDelivered supplier types (keys beginning 0S and others; see the scope item)Manage Condition Contracts - SuppliersWB2R_SV
    Commission, royaltyDelivered types in their scope itemsas per partner categoryWB2R_SV or WB2R_SC by partner category

    All are maintained in the same transaction WCOCO; the contract type decides the screens. Look up the exact keys in the scope item documents for your release.

    Split and two-step settlement
    • Split to eligible partners. In a multi-customer contract, split criteria tell settlement to create one settlement document per store, with each store's share.
    • Two-step settlement. For very large contracts, step one creates many small settlement documents (for example per store or per plant) without posting to the partner; step two collects them into one posting. This spreads the workload and gives detail.
    • Transfer of extra fields. A "transfer manager" setting can carry fields from the business volume (such as profit centre or product group) into the settlement document, so the cost lands in the right segment in profitability reports.

    Settlement · Chapter 7

    Running it day to day

    Contracts are renewed, rates change mid-year, invoices arrive late and periods close. Here is what the support team does through the year.

    Business scenario It is 28 March. The finance head wants to know: are all rebates for the year accrued? Sales wants every distributor contract renewed for next year with the same terms. And Sharma's rate was raised in January by a signed amendment that nobody entered.

    The yearly rhythm

    WhenWhatWho
    Every nightSettlement job: settles whatever is due in any released contractSystem
    Every month-endDelta accruals; review list of contracts with errors; compare accrual account with open contractsSales admin with finance
    Every quarter-endCheck run of partial settlements, approval, live run, credit notes sentSales admin, sales head
    Year-endFinal settlement; extension of contracts; clean-up of accruals on ended contractsSales admin with finance
    Any timeNew contracts, changes, customer questions about volumeSales admin

    Changing a running contract

    ChangeHowEffect
    Rate raised for the whole yearChange the rebate condition in the contractThe next partial or final settlement recalculates from the start and pays the difference
    Rate raised from 1 January onlyGive the old condition line an end date of 31 December; add a new line from 1 JanuaryEach period is calculated with its own rate
    Accrual rate changedChange the accrual conditionNew invoices use it; the next delta accruals run corrects earlier months
    A product group added or removedChange the business volume selection linesApplies from the next calculation, for the whole period
    DisputeSet the contract to "locked for settlement"Nothing is paid until released; accruals continue

    This is the answer to Sharma's forgotten amendment: enter the new line now with validity from 1 January. The final settlement on 31 March pays it correctly without any manual credit.

    Renewing contracts

    The extension function copies a contract into the next period: same partner, same selection, same conditions, new dates and a new calendar. It can run for many contracts at once. Review rates before or after, as sales prefers. Extension keeps the link between the old and the new contract, which helps when a late invoice needs a delta settlement on last year's contract.

    Year-end questions from finance

    QuestionHow to answer
    Are all rebates accrued?Run delta accruals for all contracts with the last day of the year. Then the accrual account equals expected rebates.
    Which contracts are not yet finally settled?List of settlement calendar dates that are due and open
    Why is there still a balance on the accrual account for an ended contract?Accrual rate was higher than the final rebate. The final settlement or the accrual clean-up run releases the rest.
    What will we pay in April?Check run of the final settlement for all contracts

    Settle, check run, delta accrualsSettle Condition Contracts - Customers; WB2R_SC
    Business volume listFrom the contract; WB2R_BUSVOL

    Settlement documents: display, reverse, release to accountingManage Settlement Documents

    Troubleshooting catalogue
    SymptomLikely causeFix
    Customer says volume is wrongDifferent definition, or selection lines incompleteSend the business volume list; correct selection lines if the deal letter says so
    Nightly job skipped a contractLocked, not released, or an error in an earlier date that must be settled firstRead the job log; fix the earliest open date first
    Settlement document exists but no posting in accountingBlocked for accounting: account missing, period closed, or approval pendingFix and release to accounting
    Accrual account does not go to zero after final settlementAccruals posted by a route that the reversal does not see (manual journals), or a different rateNever post rebate accruals by hand; run the clean-up; reconcile once with finance
    Rebate paid twiceA manual credit memo was also created in salesStop manual rebate credits once contracts are live
    Wrong tax on credit noteSettlement material tax class, or contract type variant not matching the tax treatmentReview with tax adviser; adjust material or type
    Very long run times at year-endHuge contracts settled in one pieceSplit by contract, run in parallel jobs, consider two-step settlement
