    Settlement · Chapter 8

    Putting it together: design and migration

    How to turn a pile of deal letters into a small set of contract types, and how to move from the old system without paying anyone twice.

    Business scenario Cocoa Crest has 140 deals in spreadsheets and old rebate agreements. Go-live is 1 April. Some deals run by calendar year and will be half-way through. The project manager asks for a plan.

    Step 1: sort the deals

    Read every deal and fill one line per deal: partner, period, which sales count, what is measured (value or quantity), rate and steps, how often paid, how paid. You will find that 140 deals fall into a handful of patterns.

    Pattern foundCountSolution
    Yearly % on all purchases, with steps, paid quarterly95Contract type ZS01, one template
    Same, for a buying group12Contract type ZS02 with eligible partners or hierarchy
    ₹ per carton on selected products for a promotion period25ZS01 with a quantity-based condition and short validity
    Growth bonus: % only on growth over last year6Needs a design decision: comparison with last year is not a simple scale
    One-off lump sums2Fixed-amount condition, or keep as a manual credit

    Step 2: decide the rules once

    DecisionUsual choiceOwner
    Definition of business volumeNet invoice value before tax, returns deducted, billing dateSales head and finance
    Accrual method and rateOn invoice at the expected rate, plus monthly delta accrualsFinance
    How rebate is shown in accountsReduction of revenueFinance
    Tax treatment of the credit noteAs advisedTax adviser
    Who enters, who releasesSales admin enters, sales head releases through workflowSales head
    Settlement rhythmNightly job; quarter-end check run reviewed before live runSales admin
    How credit is givenCredit on account, offset against the next paymentFinance

    Step 3: move without paying twice

    Situation at go-liveWhat to do
    Deal starts on or after go-liveCreate a condition contract. Nothing else.
    Deal ended before go-live, fully paidNothing. Keep the old records for audit.
    Deal ended before go-live, not yet paidSettle it in the old system before cutover, or pay it as a manual credit and document it
    Deal is half-way (for example calendar year, go-live 1 April)Create a condition contract valid from the deal's start. Bring in the business volume of the old months and the amounts already paid, so that the final settlement sees the whole year.
    Converted system with old rebate agreements still openThey may run to their end date and be settled the old way; they cannot be extended. Create condition contracts for the following period.

    For half-way deals on a new system, the old months' invoices do not exist in S/4HANA. Options, simplest first: (a) settle the old months finally in the old system and start a fresh contract from go-live with adjusted steps; (b) load the old months' volume as summary records the contract can read and enter earlier payments as already settled. Option (a) is safer whenever the customer accepts it.

    The one rule at cutover For every deal, exactly one system pays for each month. Write the cut-over month next to each deal in the migration sheet and have finance sign it.

    Roles after go-live

    RoleDoes
    Sales administratorCreates and changes contracts; answers volume questions; runs check runs
    Sales headReleases contracts and large settlements
    FinanceSets accrual rates; reconciles the accrual account monthly; owns posting dates
    Support consultantWatches job logs; fixes pricing and account errors

    Project kit

    Workshop questions, a deal-capture template, cutover steps and a go-live checklist.

    Workshop questions for the client

    The deals

    1. How many rebate, bonus, commission and royalty deals are active? Where are they recorded today?
    2. Can we see ten real deal letters, including the most complicated one?
    3. Are deals per customer, per buying group, per customer hierarchy level?
    4. What is measured: value, cartons, kilograms, growth over last year, range of products bought?
    5. Are there steps? Does a step apply to the whole volume or only the part above it?
    6. Which products or invoice types are excluded?
    7. Do deals follow the financial year, calendar year, or promotion periods?
    8. How often are deals signed late and backdated?

    Payment and accounting

    1. How often do you pay: monthly, quarterly, yearly? As credit on account, cheque, or free goods?
    2. Do you set money aside monthly today? At what rate? Who decides it?
    3. Where should rebates appear in the profit statement?
    4. What is the tax treatment of rebate credit notes? Has the tax adviser confirmed?
    5. Who approves a contract? Who approves a payout?

    Operations

    1. How do customers query their volume today? How long does an answer take?
    2. What goes wrong most often: wrong volume, late payment, double payment?
    3. Which deals will be half-way at go-live?

    Returns · Chapter 0

    Start here: goods come back

    A return is a sale running backwards, with extra questions: where should the goods go, what state are they in, and what does the customer get? Advanced Returns Management answers all three in one linked process.

    The business problem

    Big Mart received 1,000 gift boxes GB-100 from Cocoa Crest. A week later its buyer calls Riya at the order desk: "I want to send 200 back. 120 arrived crushed, 30 are the wrong flavour, and 50 I simply over-ordered."

    One phone call, three different cases. For each, somebody must decide:

    1. Logistics: do the boxes come back to our depot, go to another site, go straight to our supplier, or stay with the customer?
    2. Inspection: when they arrive, are they sellable, repairable or scrap?
    3. Money: does the customer get a credit, a replacement, part of the money, or nothing?

    Classic returns and advanced returns

    SAP has always had a simple returns order: returns order, returns delivery, credit memo. It records that goods came back and that money was returned. It does not guide what happens to the goods, and the steps are not linked: the warehouse, the quality team and accounts each work from their own lists.

    Advanced Returns Management (people say ARM) adds the guidance. The returns order itself carries the plan for the goods and for the refund. The system creates the next documents by itself, and one overview screen shows every step.

    QuestionClassic returnsAdvanced returns
    Where should the goods go?Not recorded. Someone decides at the gate.A "follow-up activity" on each order item
    What state are they in?A note on paper, or a separate quality processAn inspection recorded against the return, with a code
    What happens after inspection?Manual stock postingsChosen at inspection; the system posts or creates the documents
    RefundCredit memo request typed by handCreated automatically, with the amount driven by reason and inspection result
    Replacement goodsA separate free-of-charge order typed by handCreated automatically
    Send on to our supplierA separate purchasing processLinked: the system creates the return to the supplier
    Where does this return stand?Ask three departmentsOne returns overview
    Extra licence?NoNo. It is part of S/4HANA.

    The life of a return

    StepWhoChapter
    1. Returns order: what comes back, why, the planRiya, order desk1
    2. Goods travel and are receivedDepot gate and warehouse2
    3. Inspection and decision on the goodsWarehouse or quality3
    4. Refund: credit or replacementRiya or a returns clerk; accounts4
    5. If needed, on to the supplierPurchasing5

    Words used in this course

    WordPlain meaning
    Returns orderThe sales document that records what the customer sends back and why
    Return reasonWhy the customer returns: damaged, wrong item, over-ordered…
    Follow-up activityWhat should happen to the goods next: receive into plant, send to supplier, scrap…
    InspectionLooking at the returned goods and recording their state
    Inspection codeA short key for the result: OK, damaged packaging, unusable…
    Refund typeWhat the customer gets: a credit memo or replacement goods
    Refund controlWhen the refund is decided: at once, after inspection, later, or never
    Credit memo requestThe document that asks billing to issue a credit to the customer
    RMA numberReturn authorisation number: a reference the customer writes on the parcel so the gate can match it

    Where this sits in the SAP process This chapter covers steps A1 to A10 and B1 to B4 of the end-to-end flow. Open the process flow in SAP.

    Returns · Chapter 1

    The returns order: the plan for each item

    Riya records what comes back and why, and sets two plans per item: one for the goods, one for the money.

    Business scenario Big Mart wants to return 200 gift boxes from invoice 9001: 120 crushed in transport, 30 wrong flavour (hazelnut ordered, almond delivered), 50 over-ordered. Riya must enter this so that the depot knows what is coming, the customer knows what he will get, and nobody has to ask her again.

    The idea

    Riya creates one returns order with reference to the invoice. She enters three items, one per case, because each case has its own reason and its own plan.

    ItemQuantityReturn reasonPlan for the goods (follow-up activity)Plan for the money
    10120Damaged in transportReceive into plant, inspectCredit memo, decided after inspection
    2030Wrong product deliveredReceive into plant, inspectReplacement goods: 30 hazelnut boxes, sent at once
    3050Customer over-orderedReceive into plant, inspectCredit memo after inspection, with a handling deduction

    The fields that make a return "advanced"

    Field (per item)MeaningTypical values
    Return reasonWhy it comes back. Drives reports and can drive the refund.Damaged in transit, wrong product, quality defect, over-ordered
    Follow-up activityThe first move for the goodsReceive into plant; ship to supplier; inspection at customer site; product remains at customer site
    Product receivedTick it if the goods are already in your hands when you enter the order, for example a counter returnUsually not ticked
    Refund typeWhat the customer getsCredit memo; replacement product
    Refund controlWhen and whether the refund is createdImmediately; after inspection; decide later; no refund
    Replacement product and quantityOnly for refund type replacementSame product or another one
    Return authorisation (RMA) numberReference for the customer's paperworkAssigned by the system or typed

    Refund now or refund later?

    This is a business policy, set per case with the refund control:

    • Immediately. A trusted customer with a clear case gets the credit or the replacement at once, before the goods are back. Good service; some risk.
    • After inspection. The usual choice. The refund is created when the warehouse has confirmed what really came back.
    • Decide later. Nothing is promised. A clerk decides the refund by hand after looking at the inspection.
    • No refund. Goods come back but nothing is paid, for example a recall swap already settled elsewhere.

    When the goods do not come back to you

    SituationFollow-up activityWhat happens
    Crushed boxes are worthless; shipping them back costs more than they are worthProduct remains at customer siteNo delivery, no goods receipt. The customer disposes of them. Refund is still possible.
    A high-value item; a field rep should look firstInspection at customer siteA preliminary activity. After the visit Riya changes it to "receive into plant" or "remains at customer site".
    The fault is clearly our supplier's (for example printed cartons from a packaging supplier)Ship to supplierThe customer sends the goods straight to the supplier; the system creates the supplier return (Chapter 5)
    One item per case Do not put 200 boxes with three reasons into one item. Reasons, refunds and inspections are per item. Splitting at entry costs one minute and saves an hour of confusion.

    Returns · Chapter 2

    Receiving the goods

    The truck arrives. The gate matches it to the return, the warehouse counts, and the goods go into a holding stock until someone has looked at them.

    Business scenario Three days later a truck from Big Mart stands at the factory depot with two pallets. The driver's note shows an RMA number. Arjun's team must receive it quickly and correctly: 200 boxes were announced, but they count only 195.

    The idea

    The returns delivery that the system created from Riya's order is the warehouse's worklist. It says: Big Mart, RMA number, three items, 120 + 30 + 50 boxes of GB-100. The team finds it by the RMA number, counts, corrects the quantity to what really arrived, and posts goods receipt.

    Where the stock goes

    Returned goods must not become sellable just because they are back in the building. On goods receipt they go into a holding stock, separate from the normal sellable stock. Nobody can promise or pick them. They stay there until the inspection decides.

    StockMeaningCan it be sold?
    Returns / blocked stockBack from the customer, not yet inspected or decidedNo
    Unrestricted (free available) stockNormal sellable stockYes
    ScrapWritten offNo

    In our depot: after goods receipt, 195 boxes sit in the returns storage location in blocked status. The availability check for new sales orders ignores them.

    Whose stock is it, and at what value?

    Finance decides whether returned goods count in the company's stock value from the moment of receipt, or only after inspection has shown they are worth something. S/4HANA supports both. Valuing only after inspection avoids showing crushed boxes as assets for a few days.

    Short and over deliveries

    Arjun's team counted 195, not 200. They change the delivery quantity of the item that is short (5 crushed boxes missing) before posting goods receipt. The returns order then shows 115 received against 120 announced. The refund follows the received quantity, not the announced one. Riya sees the difference in the returns overview and can tell Big Mart.

    The RMA number is the key at the gate Ask customers to write it on every pallet label and delivery note. Without it the gate must search by customer and guess. With it, receiving takes one scan.

    Returns that do not arrive at your depot

    • Ship to other plant. The goods arrive at depot A but belong in the central returns centre B. After receipt in A, the system creates a stock transfer to B. Inspection can happen in A, in B, or both.
    • Direct to supplier. Nothing arrives at your gate. The supplier confirms receipt, and that confirmation plays the role of the goods receipt (Chapter 5).
    • Remains at customer. No delivery at all.

    Returns · Chapter 3

    Inspection: look, record, decide

    Someone opens the boxes. What they record decides both where the goods go next and how much the customer gets back.

    Business scenario Kavita, the returns inspector, has 195 boxes in the returns cage. Of the 115 "crushed" ones, 100 are really crushed and 15 are perfect. The 30 almond boxes are perfect. Of the 50 over-ordered boxes, 40 are perfect and 10 have torn sleeves that can be re-sleeved.

    The idea

    Kavita opens the inspection screen for the returns delivery. For each item she records what she found. If an item is mixed, she splits it: part with one result, part with another. For every part she chooses two things:

    • an inspection code: the state of the goods;
    • a follow-up activity: what to do with them now.
    From order itemQuantityInspection codeFollow-up activity
    10 (damaged)100UnusableTransfer to scrap
    10 (damaged)15OK, as newTransfer to free available stock
    20 (wrong flavour)30OK, as newTransfer to free available stock
    30 (over-ordered)40OK, as newTransfer to free available stock
    30 (over-ordered)10Packaging damagedShip to other plant (re-pack centre) or keep blocked for rework

    When she saves, the system does the stock postings itself: 100 boxes are scrapped, 85 move to sellable stock and are available for sales orders at once, 10 go on to the re-pack centre.

    Follow-up activities after inspection

    ActivityWhat the system does
    Transfer to free available stockTransfer posting from returns stock to unrestricted stock
    Transfer to scrapScrapping posting; value written off to the scrap account
    Ship to other plantCreates a returns stock transport order and its delivery to the other plant
    Ship to supplierCreates a returns purchase order to the supplier (Chapter 5)
    Send back to customerCreates a delivery back to the customer, for example when the claim is rejected
    In-house repairHands over to a repair process (where service functions are used)

    Why the inspection also matters for the money

    The inspection result travels back to the returns order. If the refund control was "after inspection", the refund is now created. The amount can depend on the result:

    • Item 10: 100 really crushed → full credit. 15 perfect boxes that were claimed as crushed → company policy decides: full credit as goodwill, or a deduction.
    • Item 30: over-ordered and perfect → credit less 20% handling. Torn sleeves → credit less 50%.

    Chapter 4 shows how these percentages are set once so that no clerk has to work them out.

    Who may decide what

    Not every warehouse worker should be able to scrap goods or send them to a supplier. An inspection profile per user group limits which follow-up activities a person may propose and which they may confirm. A typical setup: inspectors may propose anything; scrapping and supplier returns need confirmation by a supervisor.

    Inspect fast Until inspection is saved, good stock is locked away and the customer waits for money. Measure "days from goods receipt to inspection" and keep it under two. For products with a short shelf life, such as chocolate in summer, it is the difference between resale and scrap.

    Go deeper

    App walkthrough: record the inspection

    App: Enter Inspection Results - From Warehouse (transaction MSR_INSPWH).

    StepActionExample
    1Select by returns delivery, RMA, product or plantBig Mart's returns delivery
    2Item 10: splitQuantity 100 and quantity 15
    3For each part: inspection code, comment"Unusable"; "OK, as new"
    4For each part: follow-up activity0012 Transfer to Scrap; 0011 Transfer to Free Available Stock
    5If "ship to other plant" or "ship to supplier": enter plant or supplierRe-pack centre plant
    6SaveStock postings and follow-on documents are created
    7Returns overviewInspection complete; logistics steps listed with document numbers; refund step now due

    If the goods were inspected by a field rep at the customer, or the customer's own report is accepted, the inspection result can be entered directly in the returns order instead.

    Automatic inspection

    For low-value returns, companies skip the manual look. Recent releases offer an automatic inspection: when goods receipt is posted, the system records a default inspection code and a default next activity, for example "OK, transfer to free stock". Conditions in the standard: the item's activity is Receive into Plant and the product was not already marked as received. It is switched on per returns order type, with default values per combination of settings.

    Use it only where the business truly accepts returns unseen.

    Saved, but no stock posting or follow-on documentActivity needs confirmation by a supervisor; or refund control "decide later / no refund" behaves differently in some versions; or a posting errorCheck the returns overview for the pending step and its message

    Returns · Chapter 4

    Refund: credit or replacement

    The customer gets money back or new goods. How much, and when, follows rules you set once.

    Business scenario Inspection is saved. Big Mart paid ₹500 a box. Company policy: transport damage and our mistakes are credited in full. Over-ordered goods in perfect state are credited less 20% handling; with damaged packaging, less 50%. Goods claimed as damaged but found perfect are treated like over-ordered goods. Riya wants the system to work out the credit.

    Two refund types

    Refund typeWhat the system createsCustomer receives
    Credit memoA credit memo request linked to the returns order; billing turns it into a credit memoA credit on his account
    Replacement productA free-of-charge replacement order (a "subsequent delivery free of charge"), then a normal outbound deliveryNew goods, no invoice value

    The refund calculation for Big Mart

    CaseBoxesPolicyCredit per boxCredit
    Really crushed in transport100100%₹500₹50,000
    Claimed crushed, found perfect1580%₹400₹6,000
    Wrong flavour30Replacement already sentnone₹0
    Over-ordered, perfect4080%₹400₹16,000
    Over-ordered, torn sleeve1050%₹250₹5,000
    Announced but never arrived5Nothing receivednone₹0
    Total credit before tax₹77,000

    How the system knows the percentage: the refund code

    A refund code is a short key such as "100", "080", "050". It is a field on the credit memo request item, and pricing reads it: a condition record says "refund code 080 → 80% of the original price".

    The refund code can be proposed automatically from the combination of return reason and inspection code:

    Return reasonInspection codeProposed refund code
    Damaged in transitUnusable100
    Damaged in transitOK, as new080
    Over-orderedOK, as new080
    Over-orderedPackaging damaged050
    Wrong product deliveredany100

    The policy is typed once into this table. The clerk can still overrule a proposal for goodwill, if her authorisation allows.

    Refund determination: the clerk's screen

    For items with "decide later", or to review proposals, a returns clerk opens the refund determination screen. It shows each order item with its inspection splits, quantities, codes and proposed amounts. She confirms, changes a refund code, switches an item from credit to replacement, or rejects the refund with a reason. Saving creates the credit memo request.

    From request to money

    1. The credit memo request may carry a billing block, so that a supervisor approves it first. An approval workflow can be used.
    2. Billing creates the credit memo from the request. It posts to the customer's account and reverses revenue.
    3. The credit memo prints with tax, referring to the original invoice.
    Replacement before return: know the risk Item 20 sent 30 hazelnut boxes at once, before the almond boxes were back. That is good service. It also means that if the almond boxes never arrive, the customer has had goods for free. The returns overview shows such open cases; someone must chase them.

    Go deeper

    App walkthrough: determine the refund

    App: Manage Customer Returns, action Determine Refund (classic: transaction MSR_CRD, Customer Refund Determination).

    StepActionExample
    1Open the returns orderBig Mart's return
    2Review each line: received quantity, inspection code, proposed refund code and amountItem 10 split: 100 at code 100; 15 at code 080
    3Change where neededSales head approves full goodwill for the 15: change 080 to 100
    4Reject where no refund is due5 boxes not received: quantity zero or rejection reason
    5SaveCredit memo request created; number shown
    6Remove billing block (if set) and billCreate Billing Documents: credit memo ₹77,000 plus tax
    How the refund code works in pricing
    1. Refund codes are defined in customising (key and description).
    2. A table links return reason + inspection code → default refund code.
    3. A condition type in the pricing procedure of the credit memo request reads the refund code. Condition records give the percentage or amount per code, optionally per customer or product group.
    4. The credit memo request copies the original prices from the invoice, then applies the refund condition.

    Sales and Distribution > Sales > Advanced Returns Management > Define Returns Refund Codes / Configure Default Settings for Returns Refund Codes

    Test with one invoice at ₹500: refund code 080 must give ₹400 per box in the credit memo request.

    Credit is always 100%Refund code not proposed, or refund condition missing in the pricing procedureCheck default table and pricing
    Credit memo request cannot be billedBilling block for approvalApprover removes the block

    Returns · Chapter 5

    On to the supplier

    Sometimes the fault is not ours. The same linked process carries the goods on to the supplier and tracks what the supplier gives back.

    Business scenario Lakshmi Retail returns 300 gift tins: the lids, bought from Shree Packaging, do not close. The tins are a trading good that Cocoa Crest buys complete from Shree. Kavita confirms the defect. Cocoa Crest wants to credit Lakshmi, send the tins back to Shree, and get its own money back or new tins.

    The idea

    At inspection Kavita chooses the follow-up activity Ship to supplier and names Shree Packaging. The system creates a returns purchase order: a purchase order with a returns item, which means "we send back, you owe us". From it comes an outbound delivery to Shree and a goods issue.

    The customer side and the supplier side stay linked in one overview. But they are independent in money: Lakshmi gets her credit according to our policy, whether or not Shree has answered yet.

    Three routes to the supplier

    RouteWhenGoods path
    Via our plantWe want to see the goods firstCustomer → our depot (receipt, inspection) → supplier
    Via another plantSupplier returns are consolidated at one siteCustomer → depot A → returns centre B → supplier
    DirectThe fault is obvious; double handling is wasteCustomer → supplier. Our system records it without the goods touching our stock.

    What the supplier owes us

    Supplier refund typeMeaningIn the system
    Credit memoShree returns the moneyA supplier credit is posted against the returns purchase order
    ReplacementShree sends new tinsA goods receipt of replacement stock against the same returns purchase order; no money moves

    The supplier may also inspect and disagree: "100 of your 300 lids are fine". The result of the supplier's inspection can be recorded against the return, and the supplier refund is adjusted.

    The supplier usually gives his own return authorisation number. It is stored on the returns purchase order, so our dispatch can write it on the pallets.

    Returns that start with us

    Advanced returns to a supplier do not need a customer return in front. If incoming goods fail our own goods-receipt check, purchasing creates a returns purchase order directly. Everything in this chapter applies.

    Keep customer and supplier decisions apart Do not make the customer wait for the supplier. Credit the customer by your own policy. Recover from the supplier separately. The link between both is for information and for claim evidence, not for holding up the refund.

    2Manage Purchase Orders (ME23N)Display itReturns item for 300 tins, supplier Shree; field for supplier RMA
    3PurchasingPhone Shree, get their RMA number, enter itIf "supplier RMA required" is set, delivery waits for this number

    If Shree replaces instead: change the supplier refund type to replacement; receive the new tins against the same order.

    Setting it up

    Switch advanced returns on for your order types, then translate the company's returns policy into reasons, inspection codes, activities and refund codes.

    Returns · Chapter 7

    Running it day to day

    One screen shows where every return stands. Use it to answer customers, chase open steps and learn why goods come back.

    Business scenario Big Mart's accounts clerk calls: "Where is our credit for the 200 boxes?" At the same time the sales head asks why returns doubled last quarter, and finance asks what is sitting in the returns cage at month-end.

    The returns overview

    Open the returns order, choose the overview. You see the whole chain as a list of steps with their documents and status: returns order, returns delivery, goods receipt, inspection, each stock posting, transfer to another plant, supplier return, credit memo request, credit memo, replacement order and its delivery.

    Riya answers Big Mart in half a minute: "195 boxes received on the 12th, inspected on the 13th, credit request for ₹77,000 created on the 13th, waiting for approval by our sales head."

    Daily and weekly checks

    CheckWhyWho
    Returns orders with no goods receipt after 14 daysCustomer never sent the goods; cancel or chase. Urgent if a refund or replacement was given in advance.Order desk
    Received but not inspected after 2 daysGood stock locked away; customer waitingWarehouse supervisor
    Inspected, refund not decided"Decide later" items forgottenReturns clerk
    Credit memo requests blocked for approvalMoney owed to customersSales head
    Supplier returns shipped, no credit or replacement after 30 daysMoney owed to usPurchasing
    Follow-up steps in errorA posting or document failedKey user

    Month-end

    • Stock in the returns cage: count it and compare with the system. It should be only what arrived in the last two days.
    • Credits owed to customers for returns already received: finance may want to provide for them.
    • Scrap postings of the month, by reason: a real cost; report it.

    Learning from returns

    Because every item carries a reason and an inspection code, simple reports answer the sales head:

    FindingAction
    "Damaged in transit" doubled, mostly from one carrier's lanesClaim from the carrier; review packing
    "Wrong product" comes mostly from one depotPicking process there
    "Over-ordered" spikes after promotionsReview promotion quantities and return terms
    Many items claimed damaged are inspected "OK"Talk to the customer; tighten the policy

    Customer changes his mind before shippingReject the item in the returns order; the open returns delivery is deleted
    Field visit decided the goods stay with the customerChange follow-up activity from "inspection at customer site" to "remains at customer site"; determine refund
    Wrong inspection result savedReverse the follow-on stock posting, correct the inspection
    Credit memo wrongCancel the credit memo, correct the request through refund determination, bill again
    Claim rejected after inspectionFollow-up "send back to customer"; refund rejected with a reason

    Returns · Chapter 8

    Putting it together: policy first, system second

    Advanced returns only works as well as the returns policy behind it. Help the client write the policy, then configure it.

    Business scenario In the design workshop, sales says "we always credit in full", finance says "we lose lakhs on returns", and the warehouse says "nobody tells us what is coming". You have two hours to get decisions.

    The whole picture

    Decisions the client must make

    DecisionOptionsOwner
    When is a return accepted at all?Time limit after invoice; minimum shelf life left; approval above a valueSales head
    List of return reasonsSix to ten clear reasons; no "other"Sales and quality
    Refund matrixPercentage per reason and inspection resultSales head and finance
    When to refundAfter inspection as default; "immediately" for named key accountsFinance
    Credit or replacementCustomer's choice, or by reasonSales
    Where returns are receivedEach depot, or one returns centreLogistics
    Who inspects, and how fastWarehouse within two days; quality for defect claimsWarehouse and quality
    Who may scrap; who may return to supplierSupervisor confirmationFinance and purchasing
    When goods stay with the customerBelow a value, or when unsellable anywaySales and finance
    Approval of creditsBilling block above an amountFinance
    Valuation of returned stockAt receipt or after inspectionFinance

    Classic or advanced?

    If the client says…Lean towards
    "We have a handful of returns a month, always credited in full."Classic (or the lean returns scope) is enough
    "Returns are daily business; the warehouse and accounts keep asking each other."Advanced
    "The refund depends on the state of the goods."Advanced
    "We often send defective goods on to suppliers."Advanced
    "We want to know why goods come back."Advanced

    Both can exist side by side, per order type.

    Going live

    1. Open classic returns finish the classic way. New returns from the go-live date use the advanced order type.
    2. Block the classic returns order type for the sales areas that have gone live, so users cannot slip back.
    3. Train three groups separately: order desk (order, refund), warehouse (receipt, inspection), purchasing (supplier returns). Each needs one hour and its own one-page guide.
    4. Label the returns cage and the returns storage location on day one.
    5. For the first month, review open steps every morning.
    A sign of a healthy returns process A customer who calls about a return gets a complete answer from the first person who picks up the phone. If that works, the design is right.

    Project kit

    Workshop questions, policy templates, cutover steps and a go-live checklist.

    Workshop questions for the client

    Volume and reasons

    1. How many returns per month, per depot? What share of sales value?
    2. What are the top five reasons today? How do you know?
    3. Which customers return most? Are there contract terms about returns?
    4. Are there recalls or expiry-driven returns?

    Goods

    1. Where do returned goods arrive? Is there a separate, locked area?
    2. Who inspects? How long after arrival? What do they record today?
    3. What happens to goods after inspection: resale, re-pack, sale as seconds, scrap, back to supplier?
    4. Are batches and expiry dates tracked? Must the original batch be identified?
    5. When is it cheaper to leave goods with the customer?
    6. Is a warehouse system in use?

    Money

    1. Is the refund always 100%? Should it depend on reason and condition?
    2. Do you credit before the goods are back? For whom?
    3. How often do customers want replacement instead of credit?
    4. Who approves credits, and above which amount?
    5. How do you recover from suppliers and carriers today?

    Inspection codesKey, text, allowed next activities

    Service targetsDays: order to receipt, receipt to inspection, inspection to credit

    Transportation · Chapter 0

    Start here: from delivery to truck to freight bill

    Sales promises a date. Transportation Management (TM) makes it happen: it groups deliveries into trucks, picks a carrier, follows the journey and works out what the journey cost.

    The business problem

    On Monday morning Vikram, the transport planner at the Cocoa Crest factory, has 60 deliveries to send out. Some go to the Delhi depot, some straight to customers. He must answer, every day:

    1. What has to move? Which deliveries, how heavy, how bulky, by when.
    2. How do we group it? Which deliveries share a truck, in which order of stops.
    3. Who carries it? Which transport company, at which rate.
    4. Did it go as planned? Loaded, departed, arrived, proof of delivery.
    5. What did it cost, and is the carrier's bill right?

    Without a system this lives in spreadsheets, phone calls and a pile of carrier bills that nobody can check. TM puts all five answers in one place, linked to the sales orders and deliveries you already know.

    The main documents

    DocumentPlain meaningWho creates it
    Sales order / deliveryWhat the customer gets. You know these from Sales.Order desk, shipping
    Freight unitA parcel of goods that travels together from one place to another and is never split on the way. The building block of planning.System, from the delivery
    Freight orderOne truck trip: which freight units, which stops, which carrier, which datesPlanner (or the system)
    Freight agreementThe price contract with a carrierTransport purchasing
    Freight settlement document"We owe this carrier this much for this trip." It goes to purchasing and accounts.System, from the freight order

    TM inside S/4HANA

    TM is built into S/4HANA; people call this "embedded TM". It reads sales orders and deliveries directly, with no interface to build. It replaces the old shipment function of SAP ECC (called LE-TRA, with shipment documents and shipment cost documents). SAP allows the old function to be used in S/4HANA only until the end of 2030, so every S/4HANA customer who ships goods will meet TM.

    Basic TMAdvanced TM
    LicenceIncluded in S/4HANAExtra licence
    AimDo what the old shipment function did, in the new documentsFull planning power
    PlanningManual: the planner assigns deliveries to trucksAutomatic proposals by an optimiser; load planning inside the truck
    Starting pointDeliveriesDeliveries, and also orders before a delivery exists
    Carrier choiceManual, with simple rulesAutomatic carrier selection by cost and priority; tendering to several carriers
    Freight costAgreements, rates, settlementThe same, with more complex rate structures

    This course teaches the process that works with basic TM, and marks clearly where advanced TM adds something.

    Words used in this course

    WordPlain meaning
    CarrierThe transport company that owns the trucks
    LocationA place where goods are loaded or unloaded: our plant, a customer, a depot
    Transportation zoneA group of locations treated alike, for example "Delhi region"
    Transportation laneA route between two locations or zones, with the carriers who serve it
    StageOne leg of a trip, from one stop to the next
    ChargeOne line of freight cost: base freight, fuel surcharge, waiting fee
    SubcontractingGiving a freight order to a carrier
    EventSomething that happened on the trip: loaded, departed, arrived, delivered

    Go deeper

    Releases, deployment and old-to-new terms
    ItemDetail
    Embedded TM sinceS/4HANA 1709
    DeploymentEmbedded (same system as sales and deliveries; this course) or a separate TM system that receives requirements from one or more ERP systems
    Old function LE-TRAUsage right in S/4HANA extended to the end of 2030
    Warehouse linkTM works with deliveries from stock-room, warehouse (EWM) or neither
    Old (LE-TRA)New (TM)
    Shipment document (VT01N)Freight order
    Shipment cost document (VI01)Charges in the freight order + freight settlement document
    RouteTransportation lanes, zones, default routes
    Forwarding agent (vendor)Carrier (business partner with carrier role)
    Pricing procedure for shipment costsFreight agreement, calculation sheet, rate tables
    Shipment stagesStages of the freight order

    This course is written against S/4HANA 2023, embedded TM.

    Where this sits in the SAP process This chapter covers steps 1 to 15 of the end-to-end flow. Open the process flow in SAP.

    Transportation · Chapter 1

    What has to move: from delivery to freight unit

    The delivery says what the customer gets. The freight unit says what the planner has to move. The system builds one from the other.

    Business scenario Three deliveries for the Delhi region are ready at the factory: Sharma Distributors 300 cartons, Big Mart 400 cartons, Gupta Stores 100 cartons. One carton weighs 10 kg. Vikram needs them on his planning screen with weight, volume, pick-up place, drop place and dates, without typing anything.

    The idea

    When shipping creates a delivery, TM checks whether this kind of delivery is relevant for transportation planning. If yes, it creates freight units for it, immediately and by itself.

    A freight unit carries everything the planner needs:

    In the freight unitComes fromSharma's example
    Source locationShipping point / plant of the deliveryFactory, plant 1000
    Destination locationShip-to partySharma Distributors, Delhi
    Quantity, weight, volumeDelivery items and product master300 cartons, 3,000 kg, 9 m³
    Pick-up and delivery datesDates of the deliveryLoad 10 Oct, deliver by 13 Oct
    Link backDelivery and sales order numbersFor tracking and for cost

    One delivery, one freight unit? Not always

    A freight unit building rule decides how deliveries are cut into freight units.

    RuleResultWhen
    One freight unit per deliverySharma's 300 cartons = 1 freight unitThe usual case: a delivery travels as a whole
    Split by a limitA delivery of 2,000 cartons with a limit of 800 cartons (one truck) = 3 freight units: 800, 800, 400Deliveries bigger than a truck
    Split by a propertyChilled items and normal items of the same delivery become separate freight unitsGoods that need different trucks

    The rule to remember: a freight unit is the smallest piece the planner moves. He can put several on one truck. He cannot cut one in half.

    Plan from orders or from deliveries?

    Delivery-based planningOrder-based planning
    Freight units are built fromThe deliveryThe sales order, before any delivery exists
    How far ahead can the planner see?Hours to a few daysDays to weeks
    Typical useStock is picked first, then trucks are arrangedTrucks are booked first; deliveries are then created to match the truck plan
    LicenceBasic TMAdvanced TM

    Cocoa Crest ships from stock with a short horizon. It uses delivery-based planning.

    Weights and volumes come from the product master The planner's truck is "full" by weight or by volume. If gross weight and volume are wrong or missing in the product master, every plan is wrong. Clean this data before go-live; it is the most common TM problem and it is not a TM setting.

    Transportation · Chapter 2

    Planning: freight units become a freight order

    The planner puts freight units onto a truck. The result is a freight order: one trip with its stops, dates and load.

    Business scenario Vikram sees three freight units for Delhi: 3,000 kg, 4,000 kg and 1,000 kg. A standard truck carries 8,000 kg or 800 cartons. All three customers want delivery by 13 October. Can they share one truck, and in which order should it stop?

    The idea

    3,000 + 4,000 + 1,000 = 8,000 kg. One truck, exactly full. Vikram selects the three freight units, chooses "create freight order", and gets one freight order with four stops: the factory, then the three customers.

    What a freight order contains

    PartContentExample
    GeneralType of trip, responsible organisation, statusRoad freight order, planning status "planned"
    Stages and stopsThe sequence of locations with planned arrival and departureFactory 10 Oct → Big Mart 12 Oct → Sharma 12 Oct → Gupta 13 Oct
    CargoThe freight units and their items800 cartons, 8,000 kg
    VehicleKind of truck, capacity; later the plate number and driver16-tonne closed truck
    CarrierWho drives (Chapter 3)Empty for now
    ChargesFreight cost (Chapter 5)Empty until a carrier and agreement are known
    Document flowDeliveries, sales orders, settlementThree deliveries

    Three ways to plan

    WayHowGood forLicence
    Direct creationNo planning step. The system creates one freight order per delivery automatically, through the logistics integration profile.Full-truck customers; couriers; very simple shippingBasic
    Manual planningThe planner selects freight units in a list or in the transportation cockpit and assigns them to a new or existing freight order, by buttons or drag and dropA planner who knows the lanes and handles tens of deliveries a dayBasic
    OptimiserThe system proposes trucks, groupings and stop sequences at lowest cost within the rulesHundreds of deliveries a day, many possible combinationsAdvanced

    The planner's rules of thumb, and how TM helps

    • Capacity. The freight order adds up weight and volume and compares with the truck. It warns at overload.
    • Dates. Each stop gets planned times from distance and driving speed. If a customer's date cannot be met, the planner sees it before the truck leaves.
    • Compatibility. Rules can forbid combinations: chocolate not with strong-smelling goods; chilled goods only on chilled trucks. (Rule-based incompatibilities are an advanced function; in basic TM the planner watches this himself.)
    • Stop sequence. The planner sets it. Last loaded is first unloaded, so the sequence also tells the warehouse the loading order.
    Freight order and warehouse The freight order tells the warehouse which deliveries leave together and in which order to load. Goods issue for all deliveries on the truck can be posted from the freight order in one step when the truck departs.

    Transportation · Chapter 3

    Choosing the carrier

    A planned truck needs someone to drive it. Giving the freight order to a transport company is called subcontracting.

    Business scenario Two carriers serve the factory-to-Delhi lane. Speedy Roadlines charges ₹46,000 per full truck and is usually on time. Bharat Cargo charges ₹6.50 per kg, which is ₹52,000 for a full truck but cheaper for part loads, and has trucks free more often. Vikram must pick one for the Delhi freight order, tell them, and get a confirmation.

    The idea

    The carrier is entered on the freight order. From that moment the freight order is a job for that carrier: the system can calculate the cost from the carrier's agreement, send or print the order for the carrier, and later settle the bill.

    Ways to choose

    WayHow it worksLicence
    ManualThe planner types the carrier. The system can show which carriers are assigned to the lane.Basic
    Carrier selectionThe system ranks the carriers of the lane by cost (from their agreements) or by a priority you set, respects limits such as "at most 40% of trips to one carrier", and assigns the bestAdvanced
    TenderingThe system offers the trip to one or several carriers by message or portal; they accept, reject or quote a price; the system awards the tripAdvanced

    For the Delhi truck: full load, so Speedy at ₹46,000 beats Bharat at ₹52,000. For a 3,000 kg part load the result flips: Bharat ₹19,500, Speedy still ₹46,000.

    Telling the carrier

    1. The planner sets the freight order to "sent to carrier". A transport order prints, is e-mailed, or goes electronically.
    2. The carrier confirms, often with a truck number and driver. The planner records the confirmation, or the carrier does it himself through a portal or network.
    3. The freight order now shows subcontracting status "confirmed". The warehouse can see which truck to expect.
    Carriers are business partners A carrier is a business partner with the carrier role, and also a supplier, because he will be paid. Create both roles on the same number. A carrier without the supplier role can drive but cannot be settled.

    Transportation · Chapter 4

    The trip itself: loading, departure, arrival

    The plan meets the road. Statuses and events on the freight order show what really happened.

    Business scenario Speedy's truck arrives at the factory gate on 10 October. It is loaded and leaves at 4 pm. On 12 October Big Mart calls Riya: "Where are my 400 cartons?" On 13 October the truck stands six hours at Gupta Stores because their dock is busy. Speedy's contract allows a waiting fee after four hours.

    The idea

    Each step of the real trip is recorded on the freight order as a status or an event, with date and time. Whoever opens the freight order, or the delivery that hangs on it, sees where the goods are.

    MomentRecorded asByEffect
    Truck at gateArrival at the first stop; truck number checked against the freight orderGateWarehouse starts loading
    Loading finishedCargo status "loaded" for the stopWarehouse
    Truck leavesDeparture at the first stop; freight order "in execution"Gate or plannerGoods issue can be posted for all deliveries on the truck in one step
    Arrival and unloading at each customerArrival / unloaded / departure per stopPlanner from the driver's call, or the carrier through an app or networkRiya can answer Big Mart
    Something unplannedEvent "delay" with a reason, or a waiting timePlanner or carrierCan trigger an extra charge (Chapter 5)
    All deliveredFreight order "executed"PlannerReady for settlement

    How detailed should tracking be?

    That is a business choice. Three common levels:

    LevelWhat is recordedEffort
    MinimumDeparture from our site (with goods issue) and "executed" at the endVery low. Enough to settle freight.
    Per stopArrival and proof of delivery at each customerA daily phone round, or carriers reporting themselves
    LivePositions and events from the carrier's devices through a tracking networkNeeds a connected service and willing carriers

    Answers to the scenario

    • Riya opens Big Mart's delivery, follows the link to the freight order and reads: departed 10 October 16:00, planned arrival at Big Mart 12 October 11:00, carrier Speedy, truck number, driver's phone.
    • For Gupta Stores the planner records arrival 09:00 and departure 15:00 on 13 October. Six hours at the stop, four free: two hours of waiting fee become due, without anyone arguing from memory later.
    Who posts goods issue? Decide it clearly. Either the warehouse posts goods issue per delivery and TM just reads it, or the freight order's departure posts goods issue for all its deliveries. Both work. Doing a mix leads to deliveries left open after the truck has gone.

    Go deeper

    2Stop 1 (factory): report Arrival, Loading EndCargo "loaded"
    3Stop 1: report Departure with actual time 10 Oct 16:00Execution status "in execution"
    4If configured: goods issue is posted for the three deliveriesDeliveries show goods movement complete; billing becomes due
    5Stops 2 to 4: report Arrival, Unloading End (proof of delivery), DepartureStops complete

    Statuses of a freight order
    Status groupValues (typical)
    Life cycleNew, in process, completed, cancelled
    PlanningNot planned, partially planned, planned
    SubcontractingNo carrier, carrier assigned, sent, confirmed, rejected
    ExecutionNot started, in execution, executed
    CargoNot loaded, loaded, unloaded (per stop)

    Which events are expected, and whether they are tracked inside TM or in a connected tracking service, is set in the freight order type (execution settings).

    Troubleshooting

    Cannot set "executed"Events for a stop missingReport them or use the mass function
    Delivery removed from truck at the last minuteNot loadedUnassign its freight unit from the freight order before departure; it returns to "not planned"

    Transportation · Chapter 5

    Freight cost: what the trip costs

    The system reads the carrier's price contract and works out the cost of the trip, line by line, before the carrier's bill arrives.

    Business scenario Speedy Roadlines' contract for the factory-to-Delhi lane says: ₹46,000 per full truck; ₹1,000 for each drop after the first; waiting above four hours at a stop costs ₹750 an hour; fuel surcharge 2% on the base freight. The Delhi truck had three drops and waited two extra hours at Gupta Stores. What should Speedy's bill be?

    The idea

    ChargeRule from the contractThis tripAmount
    Base freight₹46,000 per full truck, factory to Delhi zone1 truck₹46,000
    Extra drops₹1,000 per stop after the first2 extra stops₹2,000
    Fuel surcharge2% of base freight2% of 46,000₹920
    Waiting₹750 per hour above 4 hours2 hours₹1,500
    Total before tax₹50,420

    The planner presses "calculate charges" on the freight order. The system finds the contract, applies each rule to the facts of the trip, and shows this table on the Charges tab.

    Three layers of price data

    LayerPlain meaningSpeedy's example
    Freight agreementThe contract: which carrier, which of our organisations, valid from when to when, which lanesSpeedy Roadlines, purchasing organisation 1000, 1 April to 31 March
    Calculation sheetThe list of charge lines in order, like a pricing procedure in salesBase freight; extra drops; fuel surcharge; waiting
    Rate tableThe numbers behind one line, with steps (scales)Base freight by destination zone and truck type: Delhi zone, 16-tonne → ₹46,000

    If you know sales pricing: agreement ≈ which price list applies; calculation sheet ≈ pricing procedure; charge type ≈ condition type; rate table ≈ condition records with scales.

    What a rate can depend on

    • Where: from and to locations or zones.
    • How much: weight, volume, number of cartons or pallets, distance. With steps: up to 1,000 kg, up to 5,000 kg, above.
    • What kind of truck.
    • Events of the trip: number of stops, waiting time, weekend delivery.

    Bharat Cargo's contract, for comparison, has one base line: ₹6.50 per kg, minimum charge ₹12,000. Same three layers, different rate table.

    Why calculate before the bill arrives

    • To choose. Cost per carrier can be compared before the truck is booked (Chapter 3).
    • To accrue. Finance knows the freight cost in the month the goods moved, even if the carrier bills weeks later.
    • To check. When the bill arrives it is compared with the calculated amount. Only differences need a human.
    • To know the true cost of a sale. The trip's cost can be spread over its deliveries (Chapter 6).
    Get the contracts into a table before the workshop Ask transport purchasing for every carrier contract. Put them in a spreadsheet: carrier, lane, truck type, basis (per truck, per kg, per km), rate, minimums, extras. You will see that a few patterns cover nearly all contracts. Those patterns become your calculation sheets.

    Go deeper

    2Same, ItemsItem with a calculation sheet; preconditions (for example shipping type full truck, means of transport)Item 10: full-truck road
    3Calculation sheet (inside the agreement, or app Manage Calculation Sheets)Line 10: charge type base freight, rate tableRate table "Speedy FTL by zone"

    Then, in the freight order: Charges tab, Calculate Charges. The log explains which agreement and which rate were found for every line.

    Event-based lines such as waiting time need the events to be reported (Chapter 4). Start with base freight and fixed extras; add event-based charges when tracking is reliable.

    Basic TM limits how complex a rate table may be (number of scale dimensions). Very fine-grained tariffs need advanced TM or a simpler modelling.

    Transportation · Chapter 6

    Paying the carrier: freight settlement

    The calculated cost becomes a document that purchasing and accounts understand. The carrier's bill is checked against it.

    Business scenario The Delhi trip is finished. Calculated cost: ₹50,420. Two weeks later Speedy's bill arrives for ₹52,420; they charged four hours of waiting, not two. Meera in accounts must pay only what is right. The finance head also wants to know how much freight each of the three customers' deliveries carried.

    The idea

    1. From the executed freight order, the planner (or a nightly job) creates a freight settlement document. It copies the charges: ₹50,420 for Speedy.
    2. Posting the settlement document creates, automatically, a service purchase order for "transport service" with Speedy as supplier, and a service entry sheet that says "service received, ₹50,420".
    3. That posting books the freight cost and a liability: "goods and services received, invoice still to come".
    4. When Speedy's bill arrives, Meera enters it against that purchase order like any supplier invoice. The system compares.

    Checking the bill

    SituationWhat happens
    Bill = ₹50,420Matches. Posted and paid on due date. Nobody looks at it twice.
    Bill = ₹52,420Difference of ₹2,000 beyond the allowed tolerance. The invoice is blocked for payment. Meera asks Vikram. The freight order shows arrival 09:00, departure 15:00: two chargeable hours. Speedy corrects the bill.
    Speedy was right (a stop really took longer)Vikram corrects the event on the freight order, recalculates, and creates an additional settlement for the difference. Then the bill matches.

    Some companies agree self-billing with carriers: no bill is sent at all; the company pays what its own system calculated. In SAP this is evaluated receipt settlement. It needs trusted rates and reliable event reporting.

    Spreading the cost over the deliveries

    ₹50,420 was the cost of one truck with three deliveries. Cost distribution splits it by a rule, most often by weight:

    DeliveryWeightShareFreight cost
    Sharma Distributors3,000 kg37.5%₹18,907.50
    Big Mart4,000 kg50%₹25,210.00
    Gupta Stores1,000 kg12.5%₹6,302.50
    Total8,000 kg100%₹50,420.00

    The shares flow into profitability reporting, so the finance head can see margin per customer after freight. For purchases (inbound freight) the distributed cost can be added to the value of the goods received.

    Freight cost per customer changes conversations Gupta Stores orders 100 cartons at a time and carries ₹63 of freight per carton, the same as the others here because the truck was shared. Had Gupta's order travelled alone, the cost per carton would have been many times higher. Planners and sales heads start to talk about minimum order sizes once they can see this.

    Setting it up

    A basic outbound process needs five blocks of setup. Most of the effort is master data: places, lanes, carriers and rates.

    Business scenario Cocoa Crest wants basic TM live for outbound trucks from the factory in three months, replacing spreadsheets and the old shipment documents. You must lay out the setup in an order the team can follow.

    4. Freight ordersFreight order types, planning screens, output, executionTM consultant
    5. CostCharge types, agreements, rates, settlement, link to purchasing and accountsTM, MM and finance consultants

    Transportation · Chapter 8

    Putting it together: scope, design, go-live

    TM can do a great deal. A good first project does a little, well. Decide scope and licence level, then grow.

    Business scenario The logistics head says: "I want optimisation, live tracking and automatic carrier bidding." The finance head says: "I want to stop paying wrong freight bills." The IT head says: "We have three months and no extra licence budget." You must propose a first scope everyone accepts.

    The whole picture

    Other flows use the same pattern

    FlowStarts fromWhat differs
    Outbound to customers (this course)Outbound delivery
    Stock transfer to depotsStock transport order / its outbound deliveryDestination is our own plant; inbound side receives from the same freight order
    Inbound from suppliersPurchase order / inbound deliveryRelevant when we arrange and pay the truck; cost can be added to the goods' value
    Customer returnsReturns deliveryPick-up at the customer

    Basic or advanced: a decision aid

    If the client says…Needs
    "A planner assigns 50 deliveries a day to trucks by experience."Basic
    "We want to check carrier bills and know freight per customer."Basic
    "We must replace the old shipment documents before 2030."Basic
    "We want the system to propose the cheapest truck plan for 800 deliveries a day."Advanced (optimiser)
    "We book trucks days ahead, before deliveries exist."Advanced (order-based planning)
    "Carriers should bid for each trip."Advanced (tendering)
    "We need to plan how pallets sit inside the truck."Advanced (load planning)

    Licence terms change. Confirm the boundary between basic and advanced with SAP's current feature scope description before committing to a design.

    A first scope that works

    Answer to the scenario: start with basic TM for outbound trucks from the factory.

    1. Delivery-based freight units.
    2. Manual planning in the cockpit.
    3. Manual carrier assignment, with cost shown from agreements.
    4. Minimum tracking: departure with goods issue, and "executed".
    5. Charge calculation for base freight and fixed extras.
    6. Freight settlement with invoice check and cost distribution by weight.

    The finance head gets his result in phase one. The logistics head gets visibility now and a clear path to optimisation and tracking in phase two. No extra licence is needed for phase one.

    Design decisions to record

    DecisionUsual choice for a first scopeOwner
    Which flowsOutbound from the main plant firstLogistics head
    Order-based or delivery-basedDelivery-basedLogistics
    Freight unit ruleOne per delivery, split at truck sizePlanner
    ZonesBy postal code ranges matching the carriers' tariff zonesTransport purchasing
    Who posts goods issueFreight order departure, or warehouse per delivery; one ruleWarehouse and logistics
    Tracking levelMinimum, then per stopLogistics
    Charge patternsPer truck by zone; per kg with minimum; fixed extrasTransport purchasing
    Settlement rhythmPer freight order after execution; or weekly per carrierAccounts payable
    Cost distribution ruleGross weightFinance
    Where freight cost postsFreight expense by profitability segmentFinance

    Going live

    1. Clean product weights and volumes and customer addresses first.
    2. Load carriers, zones, lanes and agreements. Compare calculated cost with last month's real bills for twenty trips. Fix rates until they match.
    3. Switch on integration for one shipping point. From that day its deliveries create freight units.
    4. Old shipment documents that are open finish the old way. Do not create new ones for that shipping point.
    5. Planner and gate work side by side with the consultant for the first week.
    6. First month-end: accrued freight versus bills received, with finance.
    The test of a TM go-live In week four, pick any carrier bill. If accounts can match it to a freight order and pay it without calling the planner, the project worked.

    An outbound truck from the sales order to the paid carrier bill, step by step as it runs in SAP.

    Use this page as a map. The picture shows the order of the steps and who does them. The table under it gives, for every step, the team, the t-code and app, the reference document and what SAP creates. The walk-through also tells you what to check. The chapters explain each step in depth.

    Outbound truck with basic TM

    Walk through it, one step at a time. The chart at the top is the whole process; the step you are on lifts out of it, and its picture opens from there. Steps with a dashed edge are done by SAP itself. Use the arrows at the ends of the chart, click any step in it, or use the arrow keys.

    Step 1 of 15 · Sales / Order Desk team

    A customer orders

    Big Mart orders 400 cartons. Riya enters the order exactly as on any other day. She does nothing special for transport.

    T-code
    VA01
    App: Manage Sales Orders
    Reference document
    None (a new document). The customer's purchase order number is noted in it.
    SAP creates
    A sales order
    Check
    Shipping point and ship-to address are filled

    Step 2 of 15 · Dispatch / Shipping team

    The delivery is created

    When the goods are due to leave, shipping creates the delivery. It carries the weight and volume from the product master.

    T-code
    VL10A (or VL01N)
    App: Create Outbound Deliveries
    Reference document
    Sales order
    SAP creates
    An outbound delivery
    Check
    Weight and volume are not zero

    Step 3 of 15 · SAP (automatic)

    A freight unit appears

    Nobody types this. The moment the delivery is saved, SAP builds a freight unit: the parcel the transport planner has to move.

    T-code
    No user action
    App: Display: Freight Units worklist
    Reference document
    Outbound delivery
    SAP creates
    A freight unit with from, to, weight and dates
    Check
    One freight unit per delivery, with the right weight

    Step 4 of 15 · Transport Planning team

    Vikram plans the truck

    Vikram sees three freight units for the Delhi region. Together they weigh 8,000 kg, exactly one truck. He selects them and creates a freight order. He sets the drops: Big Mart, Sharma, Gupta.

    T-code
    Fiori app, no t-code
    App: Transportation Cockpit
    Reference document
    Freight units (which point back to the deliveries)
    SAP creates
    A freight order: one trip with four stops
    Check
    Capacity bar is not over 100%

    Step 5 of 15 · Transport Planning team

    He picks the carrier

    Two transport companies serve this route. SAP works out the price of this trip from each contract. For a full truck Speedy is cheaper, so Vikram enters Speedy.

    T-code
    Fiori app, no t-code
    App: Manage Freight Orders
    Reference document
    Freight order. SAP reads the carrier's freight agreement for the price.
    SAP creates
    Carrier and planned cost on the freight order
    Check
    A freight agreement was found; charges are not zero

    Step 6 of 15 · Transport Planning team

    The carrier says yes

    Vikram sends the transport order to Speedy by print, e-mail or electronically. Speedy confirms and gives the truck number and the driver's phone.

    T-code
    Fiori app, no t-code
    App: Manage Freight Orders: Send to Carrier, Set to Confirmed
    Reference document
    Freight order
    SAP creates
    A transport order for the carrier; status "confirmed"
    Check
    Truck number is on the freight order for the gate

    Step 7 of 15 · Warehouse team

    Picking and loading

    The warehouse picks the three deliveries. The freight order tells them these go on one truck and in which order to load: the last drop goes in first.

    T-code
    VL02N (picking)
    App: Outbound delivery; loading reported in Manage Freight Orders
    Reference document
    Outbound deliveries listed on the freight order
    SAP creates
    Picked deliveries; cargo status "loaded"
    Check
    All three deliveries are fully picked

    Step 8 of 15 · Dispatch / Shipping team (gate)

    The truck leaves

    The gate reports the departure on the freight order. In the same moment SAP posts goods issue for all three deliveries, so stock and sales figures are right.

    T-code
    Fiori app, no t-code. If goods issue is posted per delivery instead: VL02N
    App: Manage Freight Orders: report Departure
    Reference document
    Freight order
    SAP creates
    Freight order "in execution"; goods issue documents
    Check
    Each delivery shows goods movement complete

    Step 9 of 15 · Billing team

    Customers are invoiced

    Because goods issue is posted, the customers can be invoiced as usual. This does not wait for the trip to end or for the carrier's bill.

    T-code
    VF04 (or VF01)
    App: Create Billing Documents
    Reference document
    Outbound delivery, after goods issue
    SAP creates
    Customer invoices
    Check
    Runs as before; nothing transport-specific

    Step 10 of 15 · Transport Planning team

    The drops are reported

    For each customer the arrival and departure times are recorded. At Gupta Stores the dock was busy and the truck stood six hours. That fact is now on record.

    T-code
    Fiori app, no t-code
    App: Manage Freight Orders: report events, set Executed
    Reference document
    Freight order
    SAP creates
    Events with times; freight order "executed"
    Check
    Times are right, because money depends on them

    Step 11 of 15 · SAP (automatic)

    The final cost

    SAP applies Speedy's contract to what really happened: one truck, three drops, two chargeable waiting hours. The cost is known before any bill arrives.

    T-code
    No user action
    App: Display: Charges tab of the freight order
    Reference document
    Freight order and freight agreement
    SAP creates
    Charge lines on the freight order
    Check
    Each line can be explained from the contract

    Step 12 of 15 · Transport Planning team

    The trip is settled

    Vikram turns the finished trip into a settlement document: "we owe Speedy ₹50,420 for this trip". He posts it.

    T-code
    Fiori app, no t-code
    App: Create Freight Settlement Documents
    Reference document
    Freight order (executed, with charges)
    SAP creates
    A posted freight settlement document
    Check
    Cost is split over the three deliveries by weight

    Step 13 of 15 · SAP (automatic)

    Purchasing documents appear

    Posting creates a purchase order for the transport service and confirms the service as received. The freight cost is now in the books of this month.

    T-code
    No user action. Display: ME23N
    App: Display: Manage Purchase Orders
    Reference document
    Freight settlement document
    SAP creates
    Service purchase order and service entry sheet
    Check

    Step 14 of 15 · Finance / Accounts Payable team

    The carrier's bill is checked

    Speedy's bill arrives. Meera enters it against the purchase order. SAP compares it with the calculated cost. Equal: it is free for payment. Different: it is blocked until someone explains the difference.

    T-code
    MIRO
    App: Create Supplier Invoice
    Reference document
    Purchase order and service entry sheet created in step 13
    SAP creates
    A supplier invoice, matched or blocked
    Check
    Difference is within the agreed tolerance

    Step 15 of 15 · Finance / Accounts Payable team

    The carrier is paid

    The payment run pays Speedy. The freight order shows "completely invoiced". Finance can see what this trip cost per customer: ₹25,210 for Big Mart, ₹18,907.50 for Sharma, ₹6,302.50 for Gupta.

    T-code
    F110
    App: Payment run
    Reference document
    Supplier invoice from step 14
    SAP creates
    Payment to the carrier
    Check
    Freight order status: completely invoiced

    Project kit

    Workshop questions, data templates, cutover steps and a go-live checklist.

    Workshop questions for the client

    What moves

    1. How many deliveries and trucks per day, per shipping site? Peaks?
    2. Full trucks, part loads, parcels? Own trucks or only carriers?
    3. Which flows: to customers, to depots, from suppliers, returns?
    4. Special needs: temperature, fragile, dangerous goods, mixed loading rules?
    5. Are trucks arranged after picking, or booked days ahead?

    Planning and carriers

    1. Who plans today, with what tool? How long does it take each day?
    2. How is a carrier chosen? Fixed per lane, cheapest, by availability?
    3. How are carriers told and how do they confirm?
    4. What do you need to know during the trip? Who asks: sales, customers?
    5. Who posts goods issue, and when?

    Cost

    1. Can we see all carrier contracts? How are rates built: per truck, per kg, per km, per carton?
    2. Which extras exist: stops, waiting, loading, tolls, fuel?
    3. How do carriers bill: per trip, weekly, monthly?
    4. How are bills checked today? What share is disputed?
    5. Does finance accrue freight at month-end? How?
    6. Do you want freight cost per customer or product?
    7. What is the tax treatment of transport services?

    Systems

    1. Are old shipment documents in use? Any own developments around them?
    2. Which warehouse system? Which release? Which TM licence?

    Data templates

    TemplateColumns
    CarriersName, supplier number, contact, truck types, lanes served
    ZonesZone name, postal code from/to or list of cities
    LanesFrom, to zone, distance, days, carriers with priority
    Truck typesName, payload kg, volume m³, pallet places
    RatesCarrier, lane, truck type, basis, rate, minimum, validity
    ExtrasCarrier, charge, rule, rate
    Product checkProduct, gross weight, volume, units per carton and pallet

    Cutover steps

    WhenStep
    8 weeks beforeProduct weight/volume and customer address clean-up started
    6 weeks beforeCarrier, zone, lane and rate templates filled and signed by transport purchasing
    4 weeks beforeMaster data loaded in test; twenty past trips recalculated and compared with real bills
    2 weeks beforeEnd-to-end tests with planner, gate, warehouse and accounts
    Go-liveIntegration switched on for the first shipping point; old shipments stopped for it
    Week 1Side-by-side support at the planner's desk and the gate
    First month-endFreight accrued versus invoiced reviewed with finance

    Go-live checklist

    • ☐ Scope and licence level confirmed in writing
    • ☐ Products have gross weight and volume
    • ☐ Customers and plants have complete addresses and TM locations
    • ☐ Zones, lanes and truck types loaded
    • ☐ Carriers have carrier and supplier roles
    • ☐ Control keys and integration profiles assigned for the delivery types in scope, and only those
    • ☐ Freight unit building tested: normal, oversize, changed, deleted delivery
    • ☐ Freight order type, cockpit layout and profiles tested by the real planner
    • ☐ Transport order form approved by a carrier
    • ☐ Goods issue responsibility decided and tested
    • ☐ Agreements released; twenty past trips match real bills
    • ☐ Settlement creates purchase order and entry sheet; accounts and tax checked
    • ☐ Cost distribution visible in profitability reporting
    • ☐ Invoice tolerances agreed
    • ☐ Old shipment process closed for the sites in scope
